definition_zh: 怀疑；疑惑；不确定；不信任
definition_en: to feel uncertain about whether something is true, or the feeling of uncertainty itself
core_image: 心里的秤在两种可能之间左右摇摆，迟迟不落定
scene: 深夜的站台上，末班车迟迟不来，同伴开始动摇。He began to doubt that the last train would come at all.
sceneCN: 这里 doubt 是「怀疑某事是否成立」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他开始怀疑末班车到底还会不会来。

derivatives.zh: 由 doubt 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「怀疑的；不太可能的」
由 doubt 加后缀 -less 构成，义为「无疑地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 doubted 再加 -ly 构成，义为「毋庸置疑地」
由 doubt 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「持怀疑态度的人」

senses.title: To feel uncertain about something
senses.definition: to think that something is probably not true or is probably not going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事可能不真实，或某件事可能不会发生
senses.example: I doubt that the shop is still open at this hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我怀疑这家店这么晚还开着。
senses.why: Latin dubitare meant to waver between two options, so doubt is the mind standing between two possibilities and refusing to settle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dubitare 本义是「在两者之间摇摆」，所以 doubt 就是心思停在两种可能之间，迟迟不肯落定。

senses.title: To distrust a person or a promise
senses.definition: to have no confidence in someone, or in what someone says
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某人的话没有信心，不愿相信
senses.example: She doubted his promise from the very start.
senses.exampleCN: 她从最开始就不相信他的承诺。
senses.why: The same wavering motion is applied to people: when someone's words cannot steady your mind, you doubt that person.
senses.whyCN: 同样的摇摆也用在人身上：当对方的话无法让心里的秤稳住，你就会对这个人产生不信任。

senses.title: A feeling of uncertainty
senses.definition: a feeling that you are not sure whether something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己无法确定某事是否真实或正确的那种感受
senses.example: There is some doubt about the cause of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 关于起火原因还存在一些疑问。
senses.why: Once the wavering becomes something you can name and discuss, it turns into the noun: the doubt itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这种摇摆被当成一个可以指称、可以讨论的东西，它就变成名词，也就是「疑问」本身。

senses.title: A result that is not settled
senses.definition: a situation in which the result or outcome is still not decided
senses.definitionCN: 结果仍未确定、尚无定论的局面
senses.example: The result of the vote is still in doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 投票结果仍然悬而未决。
senses.why: If neither pan of the scale ever tips, the outcome stays open, and that open state is also called doubt.
senses.whyCN: 如果秤的两端始终不倾斜，结果就一直敞着口，这种「未定」的状态同样叫 doubt。

intro.en: Doubt comes from Latin through French, and its silent b was put back by scholars who knew the Latin original.
intro.cn: doubt 经法语来自拉丁语，词中不发音的 b 是后世学者依照拉丁原形补回去的。

items.en: Latin duo, two, goes back to a root meaning two; the link to doubting is the image of standing between two choices.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duo（二）可追溯到表示「二」的词根；它与「怀疑」的联系来自「站在两个选择之间」的画面。

items.en: Dubius described something wavering between two possibilities and was built on duo, two.
items.cn: dubius 形容在某两种可能之间摇摆不定，由 duo（二）构成。

items.en: Dubitare meant to waver or hesitate and became the ordinary Latin verb for doubting.
items.cn: dubitare 意为「摇摆、犹豫」，后来成为拉丁语里表示怀疑的常用动词。

items.en: Old French douted kept the meaning but dropped the b in pronunciation and spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 douted 保留了词义，却在读音和拼写上丢掉了 b。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as douten; the exact date of the earliest written use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式写作 douten；最早书面用例的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Renaissance scholars restored the b to echo Latin dubitare, giving the modern spelling doubt.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的学者为呼应拉丁语 dubitare 又把 b 补回，形成今天的拼写 doubt。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of two; the near-meaning group gathers words for not being sure.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「二」这个词根；近义组收的是表示「拿不准」的词。

entries.definition: Feeling doubt, or probably not honest or safe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怀疑的；可疑的」，与 doubt 同出拉丁语 dubius。

entries.definition: Not likely to happen, or feeling unsure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不太可能的；怀疑的」，由 doubt 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: Almost certainly; used to state something as sure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无疑地」，由 doubt 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: To believe that something is probably true, especially something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「猜想、怀疑（多指不好的事）」，语气比 doubt 更偏向「相信其有」。

entries.definition: To raise doubts about whether something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「质疑」，是公开提出疑问，比 doubt 更主动。

entries.definition: The state of not knowing what will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不确定」，指对结果一无所知的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin root duo, two, and the French stage that dropped the b.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁词根 duo（二）与丢掉了 b 的法语阶段展开。

normal.en: Dubius meant wavering between two, so doubt is a mind split in two.
normal.cn: dubius 意为「在两者间摇摆」，所以 doubt 就是心思被劈成两半。

normal.en: Old French dropped the b, and scholars later put it back to match Latin.
normal.cn: 古法语把 b 丢了，后世学者又照拉丁语把它补回去。

normal.en: No doubt and without doubt both cancel the wavering, which is why they mean certainty.
normal.cn: no doubt 与 without doubt 都把摇摆取消掉，所以两者都表示确定。

normal.en: In doubt keeps the scale open, so the result is still not decided.
normal.cn: in doubt 让秤继续悬着，所以结果尚未决定。

normal.en: A doubter is simply the person whose scale will not settle.
normal.cn: doubter 就是那杆秤始终不肯落定的人。

abstract.en: Picture two roads meeting and a walker stopping exactly at the fork.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路交汇，行人在岔口正中间停住脚步。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale that keeps trembling without tipping either way.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平不停颤动，却始终不往任何一边倒。

abstract.en: Picture a silent b standing in the word like a statue nobody pronounces.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不发音的 b 立在词里，像一座没人念出声的雕像。

examples.en: I doubt that the library will be open on Sunday.
examples.cn: 我怀疑图书馆周日不会开门。

examples.en: Her explanation left the whole class in doubt.
examples.cn: 她的解释让全班都满腹疑问。

examples.en: He never doubted his sister for a moment.
examples.cn: 他一刻也没有怀疑过自己的妹妹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「道特」——心里那条道特别多岔口，走哪条都拿不准，于是生出怀疑。

root: 经古法语来自拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆、犹豫），源头是 dubius（在两种可能之间摇摆），由 duo（二）构成。古法语丢掉了 b，文艺复兴学者又依拉丁原形补回，形成今日拼写；b 不发音正是这段历史的化石。

sensesIntro.en: One wavering image grows into four uses: doubting a fact, distrusting a person, the feeling itself, and an undecided result.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「摇摆」意象长出四种用法：怀疑事实、不信任某人、疑问这种感受本身，以及悬而未决的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale that trembles between two pans without settling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平在两个秤盘之间颤动，始终不落定。

branches.en: FACTS: the wavering settles on a statement that may not be true.
branches.cn: 事实线：摇摆落在某句话上，觉得它可能不真，即第一个义项。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the same wavering turns toward a person whose word cannot steady the mind.
branches.cn: 人物线：同样的摇摆转向人，对方的话稳不住心里的秤，即第二个义项。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the wavering becomes a nameable state, the doubt itself.
branches.cn: 感受线：摇摆变成一个可以命名、可以谈论的状态，即第三个义项。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: when neither pan tips, the result stays open and is said to be in doubt.
branches.cn: 结果线：两端都不倾倒时，结果一直敞着口，即第四个义项「悬而未决」。

branches.en: Doubting a fact and having doubts about it are the verb and noun sides of one hesitation.
branches.cn: 怀疑某个事实与心怀疑问，是同一份犹豫的动词面与名词面。

intro.en: Doubt is a whole Latin word rather than a built form, but its family is rich in Latin pieces and English suffixes.
intro.cn: doubt 整体来自拉丁词，而不是临时拼出来的；但它的词族里既有拉丁成分，也有英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin dubius, dubitare and dubium are all recorded, and the English suffixes -ful, -less and -ly attach to the borrowed stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dubius、dubitare、dubium 均有文献记录；英语后缀 -ful、-less、-ly 可以直接接在这个借来的词干上。

items.example: The numeral gives the image of two choices.
items.exampleCN: 这个数词提供了「两种选择」的画面。

items.example: The adjective is the direct ancestor of doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 doubt 的直接祖先。

items.example: The verb supplied the everyday sense of doubting.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「怀疑」的日常义。

items.example: The noun names the thing that is in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指那件存疑的事。

derivatives.zh: 由 doubt 加 -ful 构成，义为「怀疑的；不太可能的」
由 un- 加 doubted 再加 -ly 构成，义为「毋庸置疑地」

definition_zh: 怀疑的；拿不准的；不太可能的；可疑的
definition_en: not sure about something, or unlikely to happen or to be true
core_image: 眉头皱起、嘴角下压的那张脸，写满拿不准
scene: 母亲看着窗外越压越低的乌云，对出门的计划犹豫起来。She looked doubtful when I suggested a picnic.
sceneCN: 这里 doubtful 是「怀疑的、拿不准的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我提议去野餐时，她露出拿不准的神情。

pos.zh: 形容词：怀疑的；拿不准的；不太可能的；可疑的

derivatives.zh: 由 doubtful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「怀疑地；拿不准地」
由 doubtful 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「可疑；不确定」

senses.title: Feeling unsure about something
senses.definition: not certain whether something is true, right, or a good idea
senses.definitionCN: 不能确定某事是否真实、正确，或是否是个好主意
senses.example: She was doubtful about accepting the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对是否接受这个提议拿不准。
senses.why: The -ful suffix turns doubt into a full state, so the person is filled with the wavering of the base word.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 把 doubt 变成「充满」的状态，于是人整个被那种摇摆填满，这就是拿不准。

senses.title: Unlikely to happen or be true
senses.definition: not likely to happen, succeed, or be true
senses.definitionCN: 发生的可能性很小，难以成功或不像是真的
senses.example: It is doubtful that the team will finish the bridge this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍今年修完这座桥的可能性不大。
senses.why: When the scale leans clearly toward no, the wavering resolves into a judgement of improbability.
senses.whyCN: 当天平明显偏向「不」这一边时，摇摆就凝固成一句判断：事情不太可能发生。

senses.title: Probably not honest or reliable
senses.definition: likely to be dishonest, unsafe, or of poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 很可能不诚实、不安全，或质量靠不住的
senses.example: The dealer offered a doubtful excuse for the missing papers.
senses.exampleCN: 车商为缺失的文件给出了一个可疑的借口。
senses.why: Once the uncertainty attaches to a person or a thing rather than a fact, the same adjective means shady.
senses.whyCN: 当这种不确定从「事情」转到「人或物」身上，同一个形容词就变成了「来路可疑」。

intro.en: Doubtful is the English word doubt with the adjective suffix -ful, whose older sense was full of.
intro.cn: doubtful 是英语词 doubt 加上形容词后缀 -ful 构成的，后者较早的意思是「充满」。

items.en: Latin dubius described something wavering between two possibilities.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubius 形容在两种可能之间摇摆的事物。

items.en: The verb dubitare meant to hesitate, and its noun dubium named a doubtful matter.
items.cn: 动词 dubitare 意为「犹豫」，其名词 dubium 指存疑之事。

items.en: French kept the meaning while losing the b in speech and spelling.
items.cn: 法语保留了词义，却在口语与拼写中丢掉了 b。

items.en: English formed doute from the French verb and used it for both the feeling and the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语由法语动词造出 doute，名词与动词两种用法并存。

items.en: The suffix -ful was added to make an adjective; the earliest examples are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 加上 -ful 构成形容词，最早用例只能大致定在十四世纪。

items.en: The b returned in spelling, and doubtful spread from people to outcomes and to suspicious things.
items.cn: b 在拼写上回归，doubtful 也从形容人扩展到形容结果与可疑之物。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same stem; the near-meaning group separates three shades of not being sure.
note.cn: 形近组都建在同一个词干上；近义组区分三种「拿不准」的程度。

entries.definition: To feel unsure, or the feeling of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「怀疑；疑问」，是 doubtful 的基础词。

entries.definition: Certainly; without any doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无疑地」，与 doubtful 同族但意思相反。

entries.definition: Doubtful or suspicious; closer to the Latin original.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怀疑的；可疑的」，比 doubtful 更贴近拉丁原形。

entries.definition: Not known or not decided; it can describe facts as well as people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不确定的」，既可形容人也可形容情况，范围比 doubtful 宽。

entries.definition: Doubting claims that others accept, often after careful thought.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持怀疑态度的」，多指经过思考后不接受他人说法。

entries.definition: Not probable; it states probability only and says nothing about feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不太可能的」，只谈概率，不含主观情绪。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work through the -ful suffix and the two directions the base word can lean.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子围绕 -ful 后缀，以及基础词可能倒向的两个方向展开。

normal.en: Doubt plus -ful means full of doubt, exactly like careful means full of care.
normal.cn: doubt 加 -ful 就是「充满怀疑」，和 careful 表示「充满小心」是一个道理。

normal.en: A doubtful person is not empty of answers but crowded with questions.
normal.cn: doubtful 的人不是没有答案，而是被问题挤满了。

normal.en: When the scale leans to no, doubtful means unlikely, not just unsure.
normal.cn: 当天平倒向「不」，doubtful 就表示「不太可能」，而不只是「拿不准」。

normal.en: Applied to things rather than facts, the same word means suspicious.
normal.cn: 把它用在物品而不是事实身上，同一个词就表示「可疑」。

normal.en: Doubtless is its opposite twin, made with -less instead of -ful.
normal.cn: doubtless 是它的反义双胞胎，只是把 -ful 换成了 -less。

abstract.en: Picture a face with one eyebrow lifted and the mouth pulled sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸，一边眉毛挑起，嘴角向旁边撇。

abstract.en: Picture a weather vane spinning between two winds.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标在两股风之间来回打转。

abstract.en: Picture a folder marked with a large question mark instead of a title.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹，标题的位置画着一个大问号。

examples.en: The doctor was doubtful about the test results.
examples.cn: 医生对检查结果持怀疑态度。

examples.en: It seems doubtful that the shop will reopen this month.
examples.cn: 这家店这个月重新开张的可能性似乎不大。

examples.en: They bought the car from a doubtful dealer.
examples.cn: 他们从一个可疑的车商那里买了这辆车。

dict_mnemonic.text: doubt 是「怀疑」，-ful 是「充满」，合起来就是「满肚子怀疑」；再一转，就成「不太可能」和「可疑」。

root: 由 doubt 加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成。doubt 经古法语来自拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆、犹豫），源头 dubius（在两者间摇摆）。-ful 在古英语中本义就是「充满」，因此 doubtful 字面意思是「充满怀疑的」。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix turns wavering into a filled state, which then splits into unsure, improbable and suspicious.
sensesIntro.cn: 后缀把摇摆变成一种被填满的状态，这个状态再分成「拿不准」「不太可能」「可疑」三路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face wrinkled by a scale that will not settle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被「不肯落定的秤」拧出纹路的脸。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the filled state first describes someone who cannot decide.
branches.cn: 人物线：被填满的状态先形容一个下不了决心的人，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: when the scale leans to no, the adjective judges an event improbable.
branches.cn: 结果线：当天平倒向「不」，这个形容词就判断某事不太可能，即第二个义项。

branches.en: THE THING: attached to an object or a story, the same word means shady.
branches.cn: 物品线：把它安到某件东西或某套说法上，同一个词就表示可疑，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A doubtful person and a doubtful excuse share the same refusal to stand firm.
branches.cn: 拿不准的人与可疑的借口，共享同一种「站不稳」的性质。

branches.en: An unlikely plan and a suspicious offer both invite caution before action.
branches.cn: 不太可能的计划与可疑的提议，都提醒人在行动前先留个心眼。

intro.en: Doubtful is a transparent English build: a borrowed stem plus a native suffix.
intro.cn: doubtful 是结构透明的英语构词：一个借来的词干加一个本土后缀。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin dubius and dubitare; -ful is a native English suffix meaning full of.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 dubius 与 dubitare；-ful 是英语本土后缀，意为「充满」。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the ultimate source of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是词干的最初来源。

items.example: The verb gave French its word for doubting.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「怀疑」传给了法语。

items.example: Doubt is the base of doubtful.
items.exampleCN: doubt 是 doubtful 的基础词。
它把 doubt 变成 doubtful。

items.example: It forms undoubtful in older texts.
items.exampleCN: 在较早文本中它构成 undoubtful。

derivatives.zh: 由 doubtful 加 -ly 构成，义为「怀疑地」
由 doubtful 加 -ness 构成，义为「可疑；不确定」

definition_zh: 向下；在下面；沿着；减少；低落；停机；记下；绒毛；喝下
definition_en: toward a lower place, along a line, or into a weaker or lower state
core_image: 一只手把东西往地面按下去
scene: 电梯门开，人潮往楼下涌去，谁都不想再等。She walked down the stairs without looking back.
sceneCN: 这里 down 是「沿着楼梯往下」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她头也不回地走下楼梯。

pos.zh: 副词：向下；在下面；减少；低落

derivatives.zh: 由 down（绒毛）加 -y 构成，义为「柔软如绒的」
由 down 加 -ward（朝向）构成，义为「向下的」
由 down 加 stairs 构成，义为「在楼下；往楼下」
由 down 加 town 构成，义为「市中心」
由 down 加 fall 构成，义为「垮台；衰败」

senses.title: Toward a lower place
senses.definition: from a higher position to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 从较高的位置到较低的位置
senses.example: She looked down at her wet shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 她低头看自己湿透的鞋。
senses.why: The oldest English adverb came from the dative of dun, a hill, so it literally meant from the hill downward.
senses.whyCN: 这个英语副词最早来自 dun（山丘）的与格形式，字面意思就是「从山丘往下」，所以天生表示向下。

senses.title: Along a line or a route
senses.definition: along or through a road, river, or passage
senses.definitionCN: 沿着道路、河流或通道向前
senses.example: They cycled down the river path at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时他们沿着河边的小路骑车。
senses.why: Going down from a hill also means following the slope away from you, so the word took on the sense of moving along a line.
senses.whyCN: 从山上往下走，也就是顺着坡势往前延伸，于是这个词又有了「沿某条线前进」的意思。

senses.title: To a smaller amount or level
senses.definition: to a lower level, amount, or temperature
senses.definitionCN: 降到更低的水平、数量或温度
senses.example: Turn the music down before the neighbours complain.
senses.exampleCN: 在邻居抱怨之前把音乐调小。
senses.why: If down is the direction of the ground, then prices, volumes and temperatures all fall in that same direction when they decrease.
senses.whyCN: 既然 down 指向地面，那么价格、音量和温度在变少时也都是朝这个方向落下去。

senses.title: In a low or sad mood
senses.definition: sad, tired, or without energy
senses.definitionCN: 难过、疲惫或没有精神
senses.example: He has been down since the team lost the final.
senses.exampleCN: 自从球队输掉决赛，他一直情绪低落。
senses.why: A lowered body is the physical picture of low spirits, so the direction word doubles as a word for mood.
senses.whyCN: 身体垂下正是情绪低落的物理画面，于是这个表示方向的词也兼指心情。

senses.title: Not working, as of a machine or system
senses.definition: not operating, especially of a computer system or a power supply
senses.definitionCN: 不运转，尤指计算机系统或电力供应中断
senses.example: The booking system was down for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 订票系统停运了两个小时。
senses.why: A machine that is down has fallen out of service, mirroring the physical fall that the word first described.
senses.whyCN: 机器 down 就是「倒下了」，正对应这个词最初描述的那种物理上的倒下，于是引申为停运。

senses.title: To write or record something
senses.definition: to write something on paper so that it is recorded
senses.definitionCN: 把某事写在纸上以便记录下来
senses.example: Put your name down on the list by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的名字写在门边的名单上。
senses.why: Writing presses the pen down onto the page, so the direction word came to mean committing words to paper.
senses.whyCN: 写字是把笔按到纸面上，因此这个方向词又引申为把话落到纸上、记下来。

senses.title: Soft fine feathers
senses.definition: the soft fine feathers of a young bird, used to fill quilts and jackets
senses.definitionCN: 幼鸟身上细软的羽毛，可用来填充被子和外套
senses.example: The duckling was covered in yellow down.
senses.exampleCN: 小鸭子身上覆着一层黄色绒毛。
senses.why: This sense is a separate word from Old Norse, naming the soft layer that sits low and close to the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是来自古诺斯的另一个词，指贴近身体、低伏着的那层柔软羽毛，与方向义并非同源。

senses.title: To drink something quickly
senses.definition: to drink all of something quickly, often in one movement
senses.definitionCN: 迅速把某物喝完，往往是一口干掉
senses.example: He downed a glass of water and ran for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他一口气喝下一杯水，跑去赶公交。
senses.why: The drink goes down the throat in one motion, so the direction word becomes a verb for swallowing fast.
senses.whyCN: 液体是一下子顺着喉咙下去的，于是这个方向词又变成动词，表示快速吞下。

intro.en: Down has two separate origins in English: a hill word for direction and an Old Norse word for soft feathers.
intro.cn: down 在英语里有两个来源：表示方向的「山丘」词，以及来自古诺斯语表示软羽毛的词。

items.en: Dun meant hill, and its dative form dune meant from or on the hill, which became the adverb.
items.cn: 古英语 dun 意为「山丘」，其与格 dune 表示「从山上、在山上」，副词用法由此而来。

items.en: By the medieval period the adverb had generalized from hills to any lower place.
items.cn: 到中古时期，这个副词已从「山丘」泛化到任何较低的位置。

items.en: The preposition use along a road or river grew out of the idea of following a slope.
items.cn: 「沿着道路或河流」的介词用法，是从「顺着坡走」的想法长出来的。

items.en: A separate noun, dun, meant soft feathers; it entered English from Norse and is unrelated to the hill word.
items.cn: 另一个名词 dun 意为「柔软羽毛」，由诺斯语进入英语，与「山丘」那个词毫无亲缘。

items.en: The direction word extended to prices, moods, machines and writing, while the feather noun stayed concrete.
items.cn: 方向词扩展到价格、情绪、机器与书写，而羽毛名词仍保持具体。

note.en: The look-alike group all contains the down element; the near-meaning group gathers other words for lowering.
note.cn: 形近组都含有 down 这个成分；近义组收的是其他表示「降低、向下」的词。

entries.definition: On or to a lower floor of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在楼下；往楼下」，由 down 与 stairs 复合而成。

entries.definition: Moving or pointing toward a lower place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「向下的」，由 down 加 -ward 构成。

entries.definition: A sudden loss of power, money, or success.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垮台；衰败」，字面是「往下一跌」。

entries.definition: Covered with soft fine hair or feathers.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「柔软如绒的」，来自羽毛义的 down。

entries.definition: In or to a lower position than something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……下面」，强调相对位置而非移动方向。

entries.definition: To move something down or make it less.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放下；降低」，强调动作而非方向。

entries.definition: Directly under something, often in a formal or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……正下方」，语体偏书面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the hill origin of the direction word and keep the feather noun separate.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着方向词的「山丘」来源展开，并把羽毛名词单独分开。

normal.en: The word began as from the hill, which is why it always points to the ground.
normal.cn: 这个词原本是「从山上」，所以它永远指向地面。

normal.en: Prices and volume both follow gravity in this word, so down means less.
normal.cn: 价格和音量在这个词里都服从重力，所以 down 也表示「变少」。

normal.en: A down machine has simply fallen out of service.
normal.cn: down 掉的机器，就是「倒下」停止服务。

normal.en: Writing down presses the pen toward the page, which is why the phrase means record.
normal.cn: write down 是把笔压向纸面，所以这个短语表示记录。

normal.en: The feather down is a different word from the north, not a direction at all.
normal.cn: 表示羽毛的 down 是来自北方的另一个词，与方向毫无关系。

abstract.en: Picture a lift button with an arrow pointed at the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯按钮上那枚朝地面的箭头。

abstract.en: Picture a glass being emptied in one swallow.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水被一口吞下的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a duckling's yellow fluff pressed flat by a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象小鸭子黄色的绒毛被手掌压平。

examples.en: The temperature dropped sharply as the sun went down.
examples.cn: 太阳落下时气温骤降。

examples.en: Please write down the address before you forget it.
examples.cn: 趁还没忘，请把地址写下来。

examples.en: The whole network went down during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间整个网络都瘫痪了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挡」——一只手往下挡，把东西按向地面，正好是 down 的方向感。

root: 方向义来自古英语 dun（山丘）的与格 dune，本义「从山上、在山上」，后泛化为任何较低处。表示绒毛的 down 是另一个词，来自古诺斯语 dunn，与山丘无关；两个同形词在英语中合并拼写，但词源彼此独立。

sensesIntro.en: One downward gesture spreads into space, quantity, mood, machines, writing and even swallowing.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「往下」的动作，扩散到空间、数量、情绪、机器、书写乃至吞咽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing something toward the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西按向地面。

branches.en: SPACE: the basic sense is simple downward movement.
branches.cn: 空间线：最基本的意思是朝下移动，即第一个义项。

branches.en: ROUTE: following the slope turns into moving along a road or river.
branches.cn: 路线线：顺着坡走，变成沿道路或河流前进，即第二个义项。

branches.en: LESS: quantities and moods both sink, so down covers lower prices and low spirits.
branches.cn: 减少线：数量与情绪都会下沉，所以 down 同时覆盖降价与低落，即第三、四个义项。

branches.en: FALLING: a system falls out of service and a drink falls down the throat.
branches.cn: 下落线：系统「倒下」停运，饮料「下去」入喉，即第五、八个义项。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: pressing pen to paper and the Norse feather noun sit apart from the direction chain.
branches.cn: 另一条线：笔压纸面与来自诺斯语的羽毛名词，都独立于方向义链之外，即第六、七个义项。

intro.en: Down is a free English word that also works as a building block for many compounds.
intro.cn: down 是自由词，同时也充当许多复合词的构件。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the direction word is native English and the feather word came from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先：方向词是英语本族词，羽毛词来自古诺斯语。

items.example: The hill word is the source of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个「山丘」词是副词的来源。
这个与格形式变成了 down。

items.example: The Norse noun gave the feather sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个诺斯语名词带来了羽毛义。

derivatives.zh: 由 down 加 -ward 构成，义为「向下的」
由 down（绒毛）加 -y 构成，义为「柔软如绒的」

definition_zh: 在楼下；往楼下；楼下的（房间等）；楼下部分
definition_en: on or to a lower floor of a building, or the lower floor itself
core_image: 楼梯尽头那盏灯，亮在脚下而不是头顶
scene: 夜里听见门响，她披上外套往楼下走。She hurried downstairs to answer the door.
sceneCN: 这里 downstairs 是「往楼下」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她匆匆下楼去开门。

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加 stairs 构成，义为「在楼上」，与 downstairs 方向相反
由 downstairs 去掉复数词尾构成，义为「楼下的」，属较少见的书面用法

senses.title: To or on a lower floor
senses.definition: toward or on a floor below the one you are on
senses.definitionCN: 朝所在楼层的下面一层去，或位于那一层
senses.example: He went downstairs to check the boiler.
senses.exampleCN: 他下楼去查看锅炉。
senses.why: Down supplies the direction and stairs supplies the steps, so the compound simply names movement along steps toward the ground.
senses.whyCN: down 提供方向，stairs 提供台阶，两者一合，就把「顺着台阶朝地面走」这件事直接命名出来。

senses.title: Located on the lower floor
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe a room or flat on a lower floor
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指位于较低楼层的房间或套间
senses.example: The downstairs bathroom is being repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 楼下的卫生间正在维修。
senses.why: Once the compound names a level, it can stand in front of a noun as a plain label of location.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个复合词能指代一个楼层，它就能直接放在名词前，做一个朴素的位置标签。

senses.title: The lower part of a house
senses.definition: the lower floor or floors of a house, treated as one area
senses.definitionCN: 一栋房子较低的那层或几层，被当作一个整体区域
senses.example: The downstairs is warmer than the bedrooms.
senses.exampleCN: 楼下比卧室暖和。
senses.why: A place word used with the definite article turns into a noun naming the whole lower area.
senses.whyCN: 这个地点词加上定冠词后，就变成名词，指整片楼下区域。

intro.en: Downstairs is a transparent English compound of down and stairs, first recorded in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: downstairs 是 down 与 stairs 组成的透明英语复合词，最早记录于十六世纪。

items.en: Staer meant a flight of steps, and down already pointed toward a lower place.
items.cn: 古英语 staer 指一段台阶，而 down 已经指向较低处。

items.en: Stairs settled into its modern plural shape and named the steps inside a house.
items.cn: stairs 固定为今天的复数形式，用来指屋内的楼梯。

items.en: The two words were joined to name the lower floor; the earliest examples are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 两个词被组合起来指楼下；最早用例只能大致定在十六世纪。

items.en: The compound spread from movement to location, giving phrases such as the downstairs room.
items.cn: 这个复合词从「移动」扩展到「位置」，于是有了 the downstairs room 一类说法。

items.en: It also became a noun for the lower floor as a whole, often with the definite article.
items.cn: 它也变成了名词，指整片楼下区域，常与定冠词连用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stair element; the near-meaning group names other levels and directions.
note.cn: 形近组都含 stair 这个成分；近义组收的是其他楼层与方向说法。

entries.definition: On or to a higher floor.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在楼上；往楼上」，与 downstairs 结构相同而方向相反。

entries.definition: The whole structure of steps inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「楼梯（整套结构）」，与 downstairs 共享 stair 成分。

entries.definition: The open space that contains a staircase.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「楼梯井」，指包住楼梯的那块空间。

entries.definition: In a lower position, but not tied to floors of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在下面」，不限于楼层。

entries.definition: A room or floor partly or wholly below ground level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地下室」，比 downstairs 更低。

entries.definition: The floor of a building at street level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「底层、一楼」，是 downstairs 常见的具体所指。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the compound into its two visible parts and its three uses.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把这个复合词拆成两个看得见的部件，并串起它的三种用法。

normal.en: Down is the direction and stairs is the object, so the word is literally down the stairs.
normal.cn: down 是方向，stairs 是对象，这个词字面上就是「顺着楼梯往下」。

normal.en: Swap down for up and you get the twin word upstairs.
normal.cn: 把 down 换成 up，就得到双胞胎词 upstairs。

normal.en: Before a noun it becomes a plain label, as in the downstairs toilet.
normal.cn: 放在名词前，它就变成朴素的位置标签，如 the downstairs toilet。

normal.en: With the it turns into a place, as in the downstairs is warmer.
normal.cn: 加上定冠词，它又变成一块地方，如 the downstairs is warmer。

normal.en: Unlike basement, it says nothing about being underground; it only says lower.
normal.cn: 与 basement 不同，它不表示「在地下」，只表示「更低一层」。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp glowing at the foot of the stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯底部亮着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding along the banister on the way down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着栏杆一路往下滑。

abstract.en: Picture two floors drawn as two boxes, with the lower box circled.
abstract.cn: 想象两层楼被画成两个方框，下面那个被圈了起来。

examples.en: She ran downstairs when the bell rang.
examples.cn: 门铃响时她跑下楼去。

examples.en: The downstairs windows face the garden.
examples.cn: 楼下的窗户朝着花园。

examples.en: We keep the tools in the downstairs cupboard.
examples.cn: 我们把工具放在楼下的柜子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: down 加 stairs，就是「顺着楼梯往下」，所以是「往楼下」；反过来 up 加 stairs 就是「往楼上」。

root: 英语复合词，由 down（向下）与 stairs（楼梯）直接组合，字面即「顺着楼梯往下」。两个成分均为英语本族词：down 源自「山丘」义，stairs 源自古英语 staer（台阶）。整个词没有拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The compound moves from action to label to place: go downstairs, the downstairs room, the downstairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个复合词从动作走到标签，再走到地点：go downstairs、the downstairs room、the downstairs。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp at the foot of a staircase.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼梯尽头亮着的一盏灯。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: the first use describes going toward the lower floor.
branches.cn: 移动线：第一用法描述朝较低楼层走去，即第一个义项。

branches.en: LABEL: standing before a noun, it marks a room on that floor.
branches.cn: 标签线：放在名词前，它标注位于该层的房间，即第二个义项。

branches.en: PLACE: with an article it names the whole lower area of a house.
branches.cn: 地点线：加上冠词，它指整片楼下区域，即第三个义项。

branches.en: Going downstairs and the downstairs room both depend on the same floor line.
branches.cn: 下楼与楼下的房间，都依赖同一条楼层分界线。

branches.en: A downstairs room is one part of the downstairs taken as a whole.
branches.cn: 楼下的某个房间，是作为整体的楼下区域的一部分。

intro.en: Downstairs is a compound, so its parts are free words rather than bound affixes.
intro.cn: downstairs 是复合词，它的构件是自由词，而不是黏着词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; both halves are native English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中没有任何拉丁成分，两半都是英语本族词。

items.example: Down supplies the direction of the compound.
items.exampleCN: down 提供这个复合词的方向。

items.example: Stairs supplies the object being descended.
items.exampleCN: stairs 提供被走过的对象。

items.example: The plural marks the flight of steps.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾标记出一整段台阶。
这个词干出现在 staircase 中。

items.example: The staircase leads to the landing.
items.exampleCN: 这套楼梯通向楼梯平台。

items.example: The stairwell was narrow and dark.
The basement is lower than the downstairs.

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加 stairs 构成，义为「在楼上」，与 downstairs 方向相反

definition_zh: 市中心；商业区；市中心的；往市中心
definition_en: the central business area of a city, or in or toward that area
core_image: 高楼挤在河边那一小片亮得最晚的街区
scene: 周末傍晚，公交一路往低处的商业街开，玻璃幕墙反射着夕阳。We spent the whole afternoon downtown.
sceneCN: 这里 downtown 是「在市中心」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我们整个下午都待在市中心。

pos.zh: 副词：往市中心；在市中心

derivatives.zh: 由 mid-（中部）加 town 构成，义为「城市中段商业区」
由 up 加 town 构成，义为「住宅区、上城」，与 downtown 相对

senses.title: The central business district
senses.definition: the main commercial and business area of a city, usually near its centre
senses.definitionCN: 一座城市主要的商业与办公区域，通常靠近城市中心
senses.example: The old cinema stands in the middle of downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老电影院位于市中心的中段。
senses.why: In North American port cities the town grew downhill toward the harbour, so the low part became the busy centre and kept the name downtown.
senses.whyCN: 在北美港口城市，城区顺着坡往港口方向低下去，低处成了热闹的中心，于是「低城」这个名字就保留下来指市中心。

senses.title: Located in the city centre
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something in the central business area
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，描述位于中心商业区的事物
senses.example: She works in a downtown law office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家市中心的律师事务所工作。
senses.why: Once the noun names a district, it can stand before another noun and act as a location label.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个名词能指一个街区，它就可以放在另一个名词前，充当位置标签。

senses.title: Toward the city centre
senses.definition: in the direction of the central business area
senses.definitionCN: 朝着中心商业区的方向
senses.example: The bus runs downtown every twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟公交每二十分钟开往市中心一班。
senses.why: Because downtown was first a direction down the hill, the word naturally kept an adverbial sense of heading there.
senses.whyCN: 因为 downtown 最初就是「往坡下走」的方向，所以它自然保留了「朝那里去」的副词用法。

intro.en: Downtown joins down and town, and its American urban sense grew out of the lower part of a port city.
intro.cn: downtown 由 down 与 town 组合，其美式城市义来自港口城市靠水的那片低处。

items.en: Tun meant an enclosed place or settlement and became the modern word town.
items.cn: 古英语 tun 指圈起来的地方或聚落，后来变成今天的 town。

items.en: Down and town began to appear together for the lower part of a settlement; early examples are rare and dating is approximate.
items.cn: down 与 town 开始连用，指聚落中较低的一片；早期用例稀少，年代只能大致推定。

items.en: In cities such as New York the business district sat near the harbour at the lower end, so downtown came to mean the commercial centre.
items.cn: 在纽约等城市，商业区位于靠港口的那一端、地势较低，downtown 于是固定指商业中心。

items.en: The word spread to other cities and gained adjective and adverb uses alongside the noun.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到其他城市，并在名词之外发展出形容词与副词用法。

items.en: Outside North America it is understood but often replaced by city centre.
items.cn: 在北美之外，人们能理解这个词，但更常用 city centre 来表达。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the town element; the near-meaning group names other parts of a city.
note.cn: 形近组共享 town 这个成分；近义组收的是城市其他区域的说法。

entries.definition: The residential or wealthier part of a city, away from the business centre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或副词，义为「住宅区、上城」，与 downtown 方向相对。

entries.definition: The central section of a city between downtown and uptown.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「城市中段」，位于市中心与住宅区之间。

entries.definition: A settlement larger than a village but smaller than a city.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「城镇」，是复合词的核心成分。

entries.definition: The central area of a city; the usual British term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「市中心」，是英式英语中最常见的对应说法。

entries.definition: An area where offices and shops are concentrated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商业区」，强调功能而非方位。

entries.definition: The older central part of a city, often with social problems.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「内城区」，常带社会问题的含义，与 downtown 色彩不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a port city whose business streets lie lower than the houses.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子保留「港口城市商业街比住宅区更低」这个画面。

normal.en: Down plus town is literally the lower town, which was where the shops and docks were.
normal.cn: down 加 town 字面就是「低处的城镇」，那里正是商铺与码头所在。

normal.en: Uptown went the other way and became the quiet residential side.
normal.cn: uptown 往另一个方向走，变成了安静的住宅区。

normal.en: The noun, the adjective and the adverb all point at the same few blocks.
normal.cn: 名词、形容词、副词三种用法，指的都是同一小片街区。

normal.en: In Britain the same place is simply called the city centre.
normal.cn: 在英国，同一个地方就直说 city centre。

normal.en: Downtown keeps its American flavour, which is why it often appears in films and songs.
normal.cn: downtown 带着美式色彩，所以常出现在电影和歌曲里。

abstract.en: Picture towers crowded onto the lowest land beside a harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象高楼全挤在港口旁最低的那片地上。

abstract.en: Picture a bus pointing its nose down a hill toward bright shop windows.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆公交把头朝向坡下明亮的橱窗。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one small square glows while the rest stays grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上只有一小块亮着，其余都是灰色。

examples.en: Most banks have their head offices downtown.
examples.cn: 大多数银行把总部设在市中心。

examples.en: The downtown streets are crowded on weekday mornings.
examples.cn: 工作日的早晨，市中心街道很拥挤。

examples.en: We took a taxi downtown after the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会结束后我们打车去了市中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: down 是「低处」，town 是「城镇」，低处的城镇就是老城商业街，也就是「市中心」。

root: 由 down（向下）与 town（城镇）复合而成。北美港口城市的商业区多位于靠水、地势较低的一端，因此「低处的城区」逐渐固定指市中心商业区；该词义在美国英语中定型，后扩展出形容词与副词用法。无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: One district name serves as a place, a label and a direction: in downtown, downtown shops, go downtown.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个街区名兼作地点、标签与方向：in downtown、downtown shops、go downtown。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lowest streets of a port city packed with offices.
core.cn: 核心意象：港口城市地势最低、挤满写字楼的那几条街。

branches.en: DISTRICT: the noun names the whole central business area.
branches.cn: 区划线：名词指整片中心商业区，即第一个义项。

branches.en: LABEL: before another noun it simply marks where something stands.
branches.cn: 标签线：放在名词前，它只标注某物的位置，即第二个义项。

branches.en: DIRECTION: the old downhill motion survives in the adverb.
branches.cn: 方向线：古老的「往坡下」动作残留在副词用法里，即第三个义项。

branches.en: The district and the direction are the same word because people first walked downhill to reach it.
branches.cn: 区划义与方向义是同一个词，因为人们最初就是往下坡走去那里。

branches.en: A downtown office is simply an office inside the downtown district.
branches.cn: 市中心的办公室，不过是位于市中心区划内的一间办公室。

intro.en: Downtown is a compound of two free English words rather than a suffixed form.
intro.cn: downtown 是两个英语自由词组成的复合词，不是加缀形式。

latinIntro.en: Neither half comes from Latin: town is native English and down goes back to an Old English hill word.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不来自拉丁语：town 是英语本族词，down 可追溯到古英语的「山丘」词。

items.example: Down marks the lower position of the district.
items.exampleCN: down 标出这个街区较低的位置。

items.example: Town supplies the settlement being described.
items.exampleCN: town 提供被描述的那个聚落。

items.example: City centre is the British equivalent.
items.exampleCN: city centre 是英式对应说法。

items.example: Business district names the same area by function.
items.exampleCN: business district 从功能上指同一片区域。

derivatives.zh: 由 up 加 town 构成，义为「住宅区、上城」
由 mid- 加 town 构成，义为「城市中段」

definition_zh: 向下的；下降的；向下地
definition_en: moving or pointing toward a lower place, level, or amount
core_image: 一条箭头贴着纸面向下压出的斜线
scene: 山道在脚下突然折低，扶手顺着坡度一路向下延伸。The path takes a downward turn just past the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 downward 是「向下的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是小路刚过大门就转为向下。

derivatives.zh: 由 downward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向下地」，多见于英式英语
由 downward 加 -ly 构成，义为「向下地」，书面语中偶见

senses.title: Moving toward a lower place
senses.definition: going or pointing from a higher position to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 从较高位置朝较低位置去或指向低处
senses.example: A downward path leads to the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 一条向下的小路通向海滩。
senses.why: The suffix -ward means turned in a direction, so downward is simply down plus a sense of facing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ward 表示「朝某个方向转过去」，所以 downward 就是 down 加上「面朝」的意思。

senses.title: Decreasing in amount or value
senses.definition: showing a fall in numbers, prices, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 显示数量、价格或质量在下跌
senses.example: The report notes a downward trend in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出销量呈下降趋势。
senses.why: Since falling numbers move toward the ground on a chart, the direction word also describes any decline.
senses.whyCN: 在图表上，数字下跌就是朝地面方向走，所以这个方向词也用来描述任何下滑。

senses.title: In a downward direction
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning toward a lower position, mainly in American English
senses.definitionCN: 作副词表示朝较低位置，主要用于美式英语
senses.example: He adjusted the mirror downward.
senses.exampleCN: 他把镜子朝下调整。
senses.why: English often uses one -ward form for both adjective and adverb, so the same word can modify a verb.
senses.whyCN: 英语里 -ward 形式常兼作形容词与副词，所以同一个词也能修饰动词。

intro.en: Downward is down plus the Old English suffix -weard, meaning turned toward.
intro.cn: downward 是 down 加上古英语后缀 -weard（朝……转）构成的。

items.en: Dun meant hill, and its dative dune gave the direction word down.
items.cn: 古英语 dun 意为「山丘」，其与格 dune 产生了方向词 down。

items.en: Weard meant turned toward and built words such as hameweard, homeward.
items.cn: weard 意为「朝向」，构成 hameweard（向家）一类词。

items.en: The two elements were combined to describe a slope facing downward; the exact early spelling varies.
items.cn: 两个成分被组合起来描述朝下的坡面；早期拼写形式并不统一。

items.en: The form settled as downward and kept both the adverbial and the descriptive use.
items.cn: 形式固定为 downward，副词与修饰用法并存。

items.en: British usage prefers downwards for the adverb, while American usage often keeps downward for both.
items.cn: 英式英语的副词多用 downwards，美式英语则常两种词性都用 downward。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ward build; the near-meaning group compares three words for falling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ward 构词；近义组比较三个表示「下降」的词。

entries.definition: The adverbial form, common in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向下地」，英式英语中更常见。

entries.definition: Moving or pointing toward a higher place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「向上的」，与 downward 方向相反。

entries.definition: Toward home; built with the same old suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「回家的」，用的是同一个古老后缀。

entries.definition: Becoming smaller or weaker over time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的、衰退的」，强调随时间变弱。

entries.definition: Going down in level or amount; plainer than downward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的」，比 downward 更口语。

entries.definition: Moving from a higher to a lower point, often in a formal or technical tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的」，语体偏正式或技术性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the -ward suffix and the difference between the adjective and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子围绕 -ward 后缀，以及形容词与副词的分工展开。

normal.en: -Ward means turned toward, so downward is simply facing the ground.
normal.cn: -ward 意为「朝向」，所以 downward 就是「面朝地面」。

normal.en: A downward trend draws a line that slides toward the bottom of the chart.
normal.cn: downward trend 画出的是一条滑向图表底部的线。

normal.en: British speakers add -s for the adverb, giving downwards.
normal.cn: 英式英语给副词加 -s，写成 downwards。

normal.en: Upward is the exact mirror image, made with up instead of down.
normal.cn: upward 是它精确的镜像，只把 down 换成 up。

normal.en: Homeward proves the suffix is still productive in modern English.
normal.cn: homeward 证明这个后缀在现代英语里仍能造词。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow pasted flat on a page pointing at the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚箭头贴在纸面上直指地面。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase drawn as a single line sliding down to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯被画成一条向右下滑的线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a lift button with a downward triangle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按下带向下三角的电梯按钮。

examples.en: The downward slope was slippery after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后那段下坡很滑。

examples.en: Economists warn of downward pressure on wages.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告工资面临下行压力。

examples.en: She tilted the lamp downward to read the map.
examples.cn: 她把灯往下压，好看清地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: down 是「向下」，-ward 是「朝……方向」，合起来就是「朝下的」，也可直接当副词用。

root: 由 down（向下）加古英语后缀 -weard（朝向）构成，同族词还有 homeward、upward 等。down 本身来自古英语 dun（山丘）的与格 dune；-weard 在日耳曼语中表示「转向某方向」。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix adds direction to the old word down, then the direction extends from space to numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 后缀给古老的 down 加上了方向，这个方向又从空间延伸到数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pressed flat against the page, pointing at the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚贴在纸面上、直指地面的箭头。

branches.en: SPACE: the basic use describes anything pointing to a lower place.
branches.cn: 空间线：基本用法描述任何指向低处的事物，即第一个义项。

branches.en: NUMBERS: plotted values fall toward the bottom, so the word labels a decline.
branches.cn: 数字线：画在图上的数值朝底部落，于是这个词标注下降，即第二个义项。

branches.en: ACTION: the same form can modify a verb in American usage.
branches.cn: 动作线：在美式用法里，同一形式可以修饰动词，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A downward path and moving downward describe the same motion from two angles.
branches.cn: 向下的路与向下移动，是从两个角度描述同一个动作。

branches.en: A downward trend is what you see when prices keep moving downward.
branches.cn: 当价格持续向下移动时，你看到的就是下降趋势。

intro.en: Downward is a native English build of a direction word and a suffix of facing.
intro.cn: downward 是英语本族构词：一个方向词加一个表示「朝向」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element; the suffix -weard is shared across the Germanic languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；后缀 -weard 在日耳曼诸语言中通用。

items.example: Down is the base of downward.
items.exampleCN: down 是 downward 的基础。
它把 down 变成 downward。

items.example: Downward trend is a common pairing.
A downward slope is a common pairing.

derivatives.zh: 由 downward 加 -s 构成，义为「向下地」

definition_zh: 向下地；往下；往下层；由高到低
definition_en: toward a lower place, level, or rank; the adverb form of downward
core_image: 水流顺着台阶一级一级往下淌
scene: 雨水沿着屋檐汇成细流，顺着石阶一直往下。The water ran downwards along the stone steps.
sceneCN: 这里 downwards 是「向下地」（第 1 个义项）；句意是水沿着石阶向下流。

pos.zh: 副词：向下地；往下；由高到低

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -s 的形式，义为「向下的」，也可作副词
由 up 加 -ward 再加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向上地」，与 downwards 方向相反

senses.title: Toward a lower place
senses.definition: in a direction from a higher position to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 沿从较高位置到较低位置的方向
senses.example: He glanced downwards at the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝下望向山谷。
senses.why: The -s ending marks the adverb, so downwards describes the manner of a movement rather than naming a thing.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -s 标示副词，所以 downwards 描述动作的方式，而不是给某个东西命名。

senses.title: Toward a lower amount or rank
senses.definition: toward a smaller number, a lower level, or a lower position in a scale
senses.definitionCN: 朝更小的数字、更低的水平或更低的等级去
senses.example: The forecast was revised downwards by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 预测被向下修正了两个点。
senses.why: Once the direction word covers numbers, the adverb can describe any adjustment toward a lower figure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个方向词覆盖了数字，副词就能描述任何朝更低的数值所作的调整。

senses.title: From the top through all lower levels
senses.definition: starting at the highest level and continuing through every level below
senses.definitionCN: 从最高层开始，一直贯穿其下每一层
senses.example: The order was passed downwards through every department.
senses.exampleCN: 命令自上而下一级级传达到每个部门。
senses.why: A direction that keeps going down becomes a way of describing the whole order of levels, not one single step.
senses.whyCN: 当方向一直往下延伸，它就不再是单步动作，而变成描述整个层级顺序的方式。

intro.en: Downwards is downward plus an adverbial -s that became common in the Middle English period.
intro.cn: downwards 是 downward 加上一个副词性的 -s，这种写法在中古英语时期流行起来。

items.en: Dun meant hill, and its dative dune gave the direction word down.
items.cn: 古英语 dun 意为「山丘」，其与格 dune 给出方向词 down。

items.en: The suffix weard meant turned toward and produced directional words.
items.cn: 后缀 weard 意为「朝向」，构成一批方向词。

items.en: Writers began adding -s to adverbs such as downwards and afterwards, perhaps by analogy with genitive forms.
items.cn: 作家开始给 downwards、afterwards 这类副词加 -s，可能是类比属格形式而来。

items.en: Downwards was established in print, though the earliest attestations are not precisely dated.
items.cn: downwards 在印刷文本中确立，不过最早用例的精确年代不确定。

items.en: British English keeps the -s adverb, while American English usually prefers downward for both uses.
items.cn: 英式英语保留带 -s 的副词，美式英语则两种词性多用 downward。

note.en: The look-alike group differs only in the ending; the near-meaning group offers other downward adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组只在词尾上有差别；近义组提供其他表示「向下」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective form, also used as an adverb in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，在美式英语中也作副词，是 downwards 的基础形式。

entries.definition: At a later time; it shares the adverbial -s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来」，共享同一个副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: In the direction of; another British -s adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝、向」，同样带英式副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: At or to a lower position, without implying motion.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或介词，义为「在下面」，不含移动过程。

entries.definition: In or to a lower position; also a comparative adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「更低」，兼作比较级。

entries.definition: With the head first and great speed, often recklessly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「头朝下地、莽撞地」，带有失控的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks separate the -s adverb from the plain adjective and keep the level image.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把带 -s 的副词与朴素形容词分开，并保住「层级」的画面。

normal.en: The -s marks an adverb, just as in afterwards and towards.
normal.cn: 这个 -s 是副词标记，afterwards 与 towards 同理。

normal.en: Downward can do both jobs in America, but British usage splits them.
normal.cn: 美式英语里 downward 两职兼挑，英式则把两者分开。

normal.en: Revised downwards means the number was pushed toward the floor.
normal.cn: revised downwards 就是数字被朝地面方向压下去。

normal.en: From the top downwards runs through every level, not just one step.
normal.cn: from the top downwards 贯穿每一层，而不只是一步。

normal.en: The word never names a place; it always describes how something moves.
normal.cn: 这个词从不指某个地方，它只描述事物如何移动。

abstract.en: Picture rain threading down a stone staircase.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水沿着石阶一级级往下淌。

abstract.en: Picture a lift panel where every arrow points at the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯面板上所有箭头都指向地面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding down a chart line from left to right.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手沿着图表上的线从左往右滑下去。

examples.en: She looked downwards to avoid his eyes.
examples.cn: 她低下头，避开他的目光。

examples.en: The company revised its estimate downwards.
examples.cn: 公司把预估向下调整了。

examples.en: Heat rises while cold air moves downwards.
examples.cn: 热空气上升，冷空气则向下移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: downward 是「向下的」，末尾再加一个副词 -s，就成了「向下地」，和 towards、afterwards 一个套路。

root: 由 down（向下）加 -ward（朝向）再加副词词尾 -s 构成。带 -s 的副词写法在中古英语时期流行，与 afterwards、towards 同属一类；英式英语保留这一形式，美式英语多直接用 downward。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb covers three downward movements: through space, through numbers, and through a whole ladder of levels.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词覆盖三种向下运动：穿过空间、穿过数字、穿过整条层级阶梯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water threading down a flight of stone steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：水顺着一段石阶往下淌。

branches.en: SPACE: the plainest use is physical movement toward a lower place.
branches.cn: 空间线：最基本的用法是朝低处的物理移动，即第一个义项。

branches.en: NUMBERS: the same motion describes an estimate pushed to a smaller figure.
branches.cn: 数字线：同样的动作描述预估被压到更小的数值，即第二个义项。

branches.en: LEVELS: continuing downward through ranks turns into a top-to-bottom order.
branches.cn: 层级线：一路穿过各等级向下，就变成自上而下的顺序，即第三个义项。

branches.en: Physical descent and a chain of command share the same vertical ladder.
branches.cn: 物理下降与命令链条，共享同一架竖立的梯子。

branches.en: Revised downwards and passed downwards both move from a higher point to lower ones.
branches.cn: 向下修正与向下传达，都是从较高处移向较低处。

intro.en: Downwards stacks three small pieces: a direction word, a suffix of facing, and an adverbial ending.
intro.cn: downwards 叠了三个小部件：方向词、表示朝向的后缀，以及副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: All three pieces are Germanic; there is no Latin element in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 三个部件都属日耳曼语，这个词里没有拉丁成分。

items.example: Below states position rather than motion.
items.exampleCN: below 表示位置而非移动。

items.example: Lower often replaces downward in speech.
items.exampleCN: 口语中常用 lower 代替 downward。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -s 的形式，义为「向下的」

definition_zh: 一打；十二个；十来个；许多
definition_en: a group of twelve, or a roughly counted group of about that size
core_image: 蛋托里整整齐齐排满十二个格子
scene: 烘焙课开始前，老师把鸡蛋摆上台面，让学生数清楚每盘的数量。We need a dozen eggs for the cake.
sceneCN: 这里 dozen 是「一打、十二个」（第 1 个义项）；句意是做这个蛋糕我们需要一打鸡蛋。

pos.zh: 限定词：一打的；十来个的

derivatives.zh: 由 dozen 加序数词尾 -th 构成，义为「第十二的」
dozen 的复数形式，义为「几十、许多」

senses.title: A group of twelve
senses.definition: a set of twelve things, especially eggs, bread rolls, or bottles
senses.definitionCN: 十二个一组的东西，尤指鸡蛋、面包或瓶子
senses.example: She bought a dozen eggs at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市场上买了一打鸡蛋。
senses.why: Old French dozeine was built on douze, twelve, from Latin duodecim, so the word simply carries the number twelve inside it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 dozeine 由 douze（十二）构成，而 douze 又来自拉丁语 duodecim，所以这个词本身就把「十二」装在里面。

senses.title: A large but approximate number
senses.definition: a large number of people or things, used loosely rather than exactly
senses.definitionCN: 大量的人或物，只是约略说法，并非精确计数
senses.example: Dozens of volunteers turned up before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮就来了几十名志愿者。
senses.why: Because a dozen is a handy bundle, the plural dozens slid into the general sense of many.
senses.whyCN: 因为「一打」是一个顺手的打包单位，复数 dozens 就顺势滑向「许多」这个泛指。

senses.title: Used as a counting word before a noun
senses.definition: placed before a plural noun to count things in twelves
senses.definitionCN: 放在复数名词前，按十二个一组来计数
senses.example: The bakery sells two dozen rolls every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店每天早上卖出两打小面包。
senses.why: English keeps dozen unmarked after a number, so it works like a measuring word rather than an ordinary plural noun.
senses.whyCN: 英语里 dozen 跟在数词后不加 -s，因此它像量词一样使用，而不像普通可数名词。

intro.en: Dozen came through Old French from Latin duodecim, literally two and ten.
intro.cn: dozen 经古法语来自拉丁语 duodecim，字面是「二加十」。

items.en: The numeral two goes back to a root meaning two, and ten to a root meaning ten.
items.cn: 数词「二」可追溯到表示二的词根，「十」也有自己的古老词根。

items.en: Duodecim combined duo, two, and decem, ten, to name twelve.
items.cn: duodecim 把 duo（二）与 decem（十）合起来，表示十二。

items.en: Dozeine, from douze, named a set of twelve and was used for goods sold in bundles.
items.cn: dozeine 由 douze（十二）派生，指十二个一组，用于成捆出售的货物。

items.en: English borrowed the word as dozen and applied it first to bread and eggs; precise dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入作 dozen，最早多用于面包和鸡蛋；精确年代不确定。

items.en: The plural dozens took on the loose sense of many, and fixed phrases such as baker's dozen appeared.
items.cn: 复数 dozens 发展出「许多」的宽泛义，也出现了 baker's dozen 这类固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group consists of number words and derived forms; the near-meaning group names other quantities.
note.cn: 形近组是数词与派生形式；近义组收的是其他数量说法。

entries.definition: The plural, used for large approximate numbers.
entries.definitionCN: dozen 的复数，义为「几十、许多」，常与 of 连用。

entries.definition: The Latin numeral for twelve, literally two and ten.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语数词「十二」，字面为「二加十」，是 dozen 的远祖。

entries.definition: Twelfth, formed by adding the ordinal ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「第十二的」，由 dozen 加 -th 构成。

entries.definition: The exact number twelve, without a bundle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 数词「十二」，只表精确数目，不含「一捆」的意味。

entries.definition: A set of twenty, used in the same way as dozen for bundles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「二十个」，与 dozen 一样是成组计数的单位。

entries.definition: A group made or handled together, without a fixed size.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一批」，数量不固定。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie dozen to the Latin two plus ten and to the daily picture of an egg tray.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 dozen 系在拉丁语「二加十」与日常的蛋托画面上。

normal.en: Duo plus decem is two plus ten, which is exactly twelve.
normal.cn: duo 加 decem 就是二加十，正好十二。

normal.en: Old French douze still means twelve today.
normal.cn: 古法语 douze 至今仍表示十二。

normal.en: After a number, dozen stays singular, as in two dozen eggs.
normal.cn: 跟在数词后，dozen 保持单数，如 two dozen eggs。

normal.en: Dozens of turns the exact bundle into a vague many.
normal.cn: dozens of 把这个精确的「一捆」变成模糊的「许多」。

normal.en: A baker's dozen is thirteen, a little extra to avoid short weight.
normal.cn: baker's dozen 是十三个，多给一个以免分量不足。

abstract.en: Picture an egg tray with every cup filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋托，每个格子都装满。

abstract.en: Picture twelve loaves lined up on a bakery counter.
abstract.cn: 想象面包店柜台上排好的十二个面包。

abstract.en: Picture a bundle tied with string, marked with the number twelve.
abstract.cn: 想象一捆用绳子扎好的东西，上面标着十二。

examples.en: He ordered a dozen roses for her birthday.
examples.cn: 他为她的生日订了一打玫瑰。

examples.en: Dozens of people waited outside the ticket office.
examples.cn: 几十个人在售票处外等候。

examples.en: The recipe calls for half a dozen apples.
examples.cn: 这个食谱需要六个苹果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「打枕」——一打枕头正好十二个，数着数着就记住了 dozen 是十二个一组。

root: 经古法语 dozeine 来自拉丁语 duodecim（十二），后者由 duo（二）与 decem（十）合成，字面即「二加十」。古法语 douze 至今仍指十二；英语借入后既指一打，也在复数中引申为「许多」。

sensesIntro.en: The exact bundle of twelve loosens into an approximate many, and then works as a counting word.
sensesIntro.cn: 精确的「十二个一捆」先松成模糊的「许多」，再充当计数量词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray whose twelve cups are all filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：十二个格子全部装满的托盘。

branches.en: THE BUNDLE: the core sense is a set of exactly twelve goods.
branches.cn: 成组线：核心义是正好十二件货物组成的一组，即第一个义项。

branches.en: MANY: the plural loosens the exact number into a vague crowd.
branches.cn: 泛指线：复数把精确数字放松成模糊的一大群，即第二个义项。

branches.en: COUNTING: placed before a noun, it measures rather than names.
branches.cn: 计量线：放在名词前，它用来计量而不是命名，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A dozen eggs and two dozen rolls use the same bundle as a unit.
branches.cn: 一打鸡蛋与两打小面包，都把同一个「一捆」当单位。

branches.en: Dozens of people is the counting word stretched into a crowd.
branches.cn: dozens of people 就是把这个计量单位拉长成一大群人。

intro.en: Dozen is a borrowed whole word; its parts are Latin numerals rather than living English affixes.
intro.cn: dozen 是整体借来的词，它的构件是拉丁数词，而不是活的英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin duo and decem combine in duodecim, and Old French reshaped it into douze and dozeine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 duo 与 decem 合成 duodecim，古法语又把它塑造成 douze 与 dozeine。

items.example: Duo is the first half of twelve.
Decem is the second half of twelve.
The Latin numeral is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁数词是直接来源。

items.example: French kept the numeral after the noun was borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 法语在名词借出后仍保留这个数词。
这个名词变成了英语的 dozen。

derivatives.zh: 由 dozen 加 -th 构成，义为「第十二的」

definition_zh: 草稿；草案；汇票；通风；挑选；起草；征召
definition_en: a first rough version of a text, or a current of air, or to write an early version
core_image: 纸上涂改满篇的第一稿，还留着未定形的线条
scene: 会议室里，几个人围着打印稿争论措辞，纸上还画着箭头。She finished the first draft of the report at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 draft 是「草稿」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她半夜完成了报告的初稿。

pos.zh: 名词：草稿；草案；汇票；穿堂风；征兵

derivatives.zh: 由 draft 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「起草人」
由 draft 加 -ing 构成，义为「起草工作；制图」
由前缀 re-「再」加 draft 构成，义为「重新起草」

senses.title: A first rough version of a text
senses.definition: an early version of a piece of writing, not yet finished or approved
senses.definitionCN: 文字作品尚未完成或未获批准的早期版本
senses.example: He sent me a rough draft of his speech.
senses.exampleCN: 他把演讲的粗稿发给我。
senses.why: The word first meant something pulled or drawn out, so a draft is the part of a text pulled out from the mind before it sets.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早表示「被拉出来、画出来的东西」，所以草稿就是从脑子里先拉出来的那一部分文字，尚未定型。

senses.title: A plan not yet final
senses.definition: a written plan or proposal that still has to be discussed and approved
senses.definitionCN: 尚待讨论与批准的书面计划或提案
senses.example: The committee rejected the draft budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会否决了预算草案。
senses.why: A budget also starts as a drawn outline before it becomes binding, so the same word covers any unfinished plan.
senses.whyCN: 预算同样先有一个画出来的框架，之后才变得有约束力，因此同一个词也指任何未定案的计划。

senses.title: An order to pay money
senses.definition: a written order asking a bank to pay a sum of money to a named person
senses.definitionCN: 要求银行向指定的人支付一笔款项的书面指令
senses.example: The buyer paid by bank draft.
senses.exampleCN: 买家以银行汇票付款。
senses.why: A payment order is also a drawn writing, a document pulled out of an account, so banking borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 付款指令也是一种「画出来的文书」，是从账户里拉出的一纸凭证，于是银行沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: A current of air in a room
senses.definition: a stream of cool air that comes through a window or a gap
senses.definitionCN: 从窗户或缝隙进来的冷气流
senses.example: A cold draft came under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一股冷风从门底下钻进来。
senses.why: This sense is a separate English word for pulling, because air is literally drawn or pulled through a gap.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个英语词，本义是「拉、拖」，因为风正是被从缝隙里拉进来的。

senses.title: To write an early version
senses.definition: to write the first version of a letter, speech, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 写出信件、演讲或计划的第一个版本
senses.example: They asked her to draft the reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请她起草回信。
senses.why: Since a draft is the pulled-out version, the verb simply names the act of producing that version.
senses.whyCN: 既然草稿是「先拉出来的那一版」，动词自然就是「把那一版写出来」这个动作。

senses.title: To call people into military service
senses.definition: to order people to join the armed forces or to move staff to another job
senses.definitionCN: 命令人们入伍，或把人员调去别的岗位
senses.example: He was drafted into the army at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁时被征召入伍。
senses.why: People are pulled out of ordinary life the way a plan is pulled out of the mind, so the same verb serves military service.
senses.whyCN: 人被从日常生活中「拉走」，正如计划从脑子里被拉出来，于是同一个动词也用于征兵。

intro.en: Draft and draught are the same word in two spellings, and both go back to a verb meaning to draw or pull.
intro.cn: draft 与 draught 是同一个词的两种拼写，都可追溯到表示「拉、画」的动词。

items.en: Dragan meant to draw or pull and is the ancestor of modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拉、拖、画」，是现代 draw 的祖先。

items.en: Draught named the act of drawing, and then the thing drawn, such as a written outline.
items.cn: draught 指「拉、画」的动作，后来指被画出的东西，例如一份文字框架。

items.en: The spelling draft became usual for written versions and for banking orders.
items.cn: 拼写 draft 逐渐固定用于文字版本与银行票据。

items.en: Military drafting developed the sense of pulling people into service.
items.cn: 军事上的征兵用法发展出「把人拉去服役」的意思。

items.en: In Britain draught is kept for air and drinks, while draft dominates in America for most senses.
items.cn: 英式英语用 draught 指气流与饮品，美式英语则在多数义项上用 draft。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the draw root or the spelling; the near-meaning group compares words for preliminary versions.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拉」的词根或拼写；近义组比较表示「初步版本」的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling, used for air currents and drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，多用于气流与饮品义，与 draft 同源。

entries.definition: To make a picture with lines, or to pull something toward you.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「画；拉」，是 draft 的远亲基础词。

entries.definition: A person who writes the first version of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起草人」，由 draft 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A short plan showing main points only.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提纲」，只列要点，比 draft 更简。

entries.definition: A quick rough drawing or description.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「速写、粗略描述」，强调快速而非完整。

entries.definition: One form of a text among several revisions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，指多次修改中的一个形态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the pulling image behind draw and the split between draft and draught.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着 draw 背后的「拉」意象，以及 draft 与 draught 的分工展开。

normal.en: Dragan meant to pull, and a draft is what you pull out of your mind first.
normal.cn: dragan 意为「拉」，草稿就是你最先从脑子里拉出来的那部分。

normal.en: British air is a draught, American air is a draft, but the origin is one word.
normal.cn: 英式写 draught 表示气流，美式写 draft，但源头是同一个词。

normal.en: A bank draft pulls money out of an account on paper.
normal.cn: bank draft 是用一张纸把钱从账户里拉出来。

normal.en: To draft a soldier is to pull him out of civilian life.
normal.cn: draft 一个士兵，就是把他从平民生活中拉走。

normal.en: Redraft simply means draw the whole thing again.
normal.cn: redraft 就是「把整篇再画一遍」。

abstract.en: Picture a page covered with arrows and crossed-out lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，满是箭头和划掉的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain moving at the edge of a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门缝边轻轻摆动的窗帘。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a sheet from a stack of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从一摞纸里抽出最上面一张。

examples.en: The lawyer drafted a new contract for the deal.
examples.cn: 律师为这笔交易起草了一份新合同。

examples.en: Her second draft was much shorter than the first.
examples.cn: 她的第二稿比第一稿短得多。

examples.en: A draft blew through the open window all night.
examples.cn: 整夜都有风从敞开的窗户灌进来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓夫特」——把壮丁抓去当兵（draft），也把脑子里的想法抓出来写成草稿。

root: 与 draught 同源，源自中古英语 draught（拉、画），再往上追溯至古英语 dragan（拉、拖、画），与现代 draw 同源。由「拉出、画出」引申为「草稿、草案、汇票」，由「拉动的气流」引申为「穿堂风」，由「把人拉走」引申为「征召」。

sensesIntro.en: One pulling motion produces written early versions, payment orders, air currents and conscripted soldiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「拉」的动作，生出文字初稿、付款指令、气流与征兵四类用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet pulled out of a stack, still covered in corrections.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一摞纸里抽出来的一页，上面满是涂改。

branches.en: TEXT: the early version and the act of making it are the noun and verb of one outline.
branches.cn: 文字线：初稿与起草动作，是同一份框架的名词与动词，即第一、五个义项。

branches.en: PLANS: budgets and agreements also begin as drawn outlines.
branches.cn: 计划线：预算与协议同样从画出的框架开始，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MONEY: a payment order is a document drawn on an account.
branches.cn: 金钱线：付款指令是从账户里画出的一纸文书，即第三个义项。

branches.en: AIR: moving air is literally pulled through a gap.
branches.cn: 气流线：流动的空气正是被从缝隙里拉进来的，即第四个义项。

branches.en: PEOPLE: conscription pulls a person out of ordinary life.
branches.cn: 人员线：征兵把人从平常生活中拉走，即第六个义项。

intro.en: Draft is a whole English word, but it still takes ordinary English affixes freely.
intro.cn: draft 是完整的英语词，但仍可自由地接普通英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is involved; the root dragan is Germanic and shares an origin with draw.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先；dragan 属日耳曼语，与 draw 同源。

items.example: The verb is the ancestor of draft.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 draft 的祖先。

items.example: Draw and draft grew from the same root.
items.exampleCN: draw 与 draft 出自同一个词根。

items.example: British usage keeps draught for air.
items.exampleCN: 英式用法保留 draught 指气流。

items.example: Rough draft is a common pairing.
Bank draft is a fixed term.

derivatives.zh: 由 draft 加 -er 构成，义为「起草人」
由 re- 加 draft 构成，义为「重新起草」

definition_zh: 拖；拉；拖沓；沉闷乏味的事；阻力；拖着走
definition_en: to pull something heavy along the ground, or a dull boring experience
core_image: 一只箱子贴着地面被拖行，留下长长一道痕
scene: 搬家的下午，楼道里只剩一个人拖着箱子，轮子早坏了。He had to drag the suitcase up three flights of stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 drag 是「拖、拉」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他不得不把行李箱拖上三层楼。

pos.zh: 名词：烦人的事；阻力；拖曳

derivatives.zh: 由 drag 加 -ing 构成，义为「拖拖拉拉的；令人疲惫的」
由 drag 加 -er 构成，义为「拖曳者；拖网船」
由 drag 加 net 复合而成，义为「拖网；大搜捕」

senses.title: To pull something heavy along
senses.definition: to pull something heavy along the ground or another surface
senses.definitionCN: 把沉重的东西在地面或别的表面上拉动
senses.example: They dragged the broken chair to the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把坏掉的椅子拖到院子里。
senses.why: The verb began as a strong pull through soil or mud, and that heavy scraping motion is still the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最初指在土壤或泥里用力拖，那种沉重的摩擦感至今仍是核心义。

senses.title: To move slowly and unwillingly
senses.definition: to move or go somewhere too slowly, often because you do not want to
senses.definitionCN: 移动得太慢，往往是因为不愿意去
senses.example: He dragged himself out of bed at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他中午才磨蹭着起床。
senses.why: When the body itself becomes the heavy object, the same pull turns into reluctant, slow movement.
senses.whyCN: 当身体自己成了那个沉重的物件，同样的「拉」就变成不情愿的缓慢移动。

senses.title: To continue for too long
senses.definition: to last longer than is wanted or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 持续时间超过人们的期待或兴趣
senses.example: The meeting dragged on for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议拖了三个小时。
senses.why: Something that is dragged out is pulled longer than its natural length, so the phrase means prolonged.
senses.whyCN: 被拖出来的东西总比原本更长，所以这个词组表示「被拉长、拖久」。

senses.title: Something dull and tiring
senses.definition: an activity or event that is boring, slow, and unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 枯燥、缓慢又不愉快的活动或事件
senses.example: Waiting at the clinic was a real drag.
senses.exampleCN: 在诊所等候实在是一件苦差事。
senses.why: If an experience feels like a heavy load you must pull along, it becomes a drag in the slang sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一段经历像是必须拖着走的沉重负担，它在口语里就变成了「苦差事」。

senses.title: Resistance in the air or water
senses.definition: the force that slows an object moving through air or water
senses.definitionCN: 物体在空气或水中移动时使其减速的力
senses.example: The plane's shape reduces drag at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种机型在高速时能减小阻力。
senses.why: Anything moving through a medium is held back as if something were pulling it backwards.
senses.whyCN: 任何在介质中前进的物体都被向后拽住，仿佛有什么东西在往后拖它。

intro.en: Drag is a Germanic verb of pulling, probably related to draw, and it has kept a heavy scraping feel.
intro.cn: drag 是表示「拉」的日耳曼语动词，可能与 draw 同源，一直带着沉重的摩擦感。

items.en: The root behind draw and drag is usually reconstructed as a pulling root; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: draw 与 drag 背后的词根一般被重构为一个表示「拉」的形式，确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Dragan meant to draw or pull and became modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拉、拖」，演变为现代的 draw。

items.en: A variant with a doubled g described pulling something heavy along the ground.
items.cn: 一个带双 g 的变体专门描述把重物贴着地面拖行。

items.en: The noun drag named a heavy sled or a hooked tool for fishing; dating of first use is approximate.
items.cn: 名词 drag 指沉重的雪橇或带钩的渔具；首次使用的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: The word extended to slow movement, boring events, air resistance and computer dragging.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到缓慢移动、乏味之事、空气阻力与计算机拖放操作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pulling root; the near-meaning group separates types of heavy pulling.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拉」的词根；近义组区分几种「费力拉」的方式。

entries.definition: To pull something toward you, or to sketch with lines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉；画」，与 drag 同源。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of drag.
entries.definitionCN: drag 的过去式与过去分词，注意末尾要双写 g 再加 -ed。

entries.definition: A net pulled along the bottom, or a widespread police search.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拖网；大搜捕」，形象是「拖着网扫过」。

entries.definition: To move something toward you with force; it does not imply scraping.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉」，不强调摩擦，是最中性的说法。

entries.definition: To pull something heavy over a long distance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「长途拖运」，强调距离与重量。

entries.definition: To pull sharply and repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用力猛拉」，是短促反复的拉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the scraping sound and from the phrases that grew out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从摩擦声出发，并串联由它长出的短语。

normal.en: The doubled g and the hard final sound copy the noise of scraping.
normal.cn: 双写的 g 与结实的收音，模仿了拖擦时的声响。

normal.en: Drag on means the thing is pulled longer than it should be.
normal.cn: drag on 就是被拉得比本该有的更长。

normal.en: A drag of an evening is a load you had to pull through.
normal.cn: a drag of an evening 就是一整晚你必须拖过去的负担。

normal.en: Drag in physics is resistance, as if the air were pulling you back.
normal.cn: 物理里的 drag 是阻力，仿佛空气在把你往后拽。

normal.en: Drag and drop on a screen copies the hand motion exactly.
normal.cn: 屏幕上的 drag and drop 完全照搬了手上的拖拽动作。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase with a broken wheel leaving a line in the dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一只轮子坏掉的行李箱在灰尘里划出一道线。

abstract.en: Picture two people tugging a heavy sled uphill.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人拉着沉重的雪橇往坡上去。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands refuse to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针怎么都不肯动。

examples.en: She dragged the box across the floor.
examples.cn: 她把箱子拖过地板。

examples.en: The trial dragged on for months.
examples.cn: 这场审判拖了好几个月。

examples.en: Cleaning the whole flat was a drag.
examples.cn: 打扫整个公寓真是件苦差事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽个」——拽着个重箱子在地上拖，drag 就是「拽着走」。

root: 日耳曼语动词，与古英语 dragan（拉、拖，今 draw）同源；中古英语出现带双 g 的变体 draggen，专指把重物贴地拖动。由「贴地拖行」引申为「磨蹭」、「拖久」，再引申为口语中的「苦差事」与物理上的「阻力」。

sensesIntro.en: The heavy scraping pull extends to reluctant motion, overlong events, dull chores and physical resistance.
sensesIntro.cn: 沉重的摩擦式拉动，延伸出不情愿的移动、过长的过程、乏味的差事与物理阻力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy box scraping along the ground, leaving a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的箱子贴着地面摩擦前进，留下一道痕。

branches.en: PULLING: the basic sense is a heavy object moved along a surface.
branches.cn: 拉拽线：基本义是让重物贴着表面移动，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE BODY: when the body is the weight, movement turns slow and unwilling.
branches.cn: 身体线：当身体成了那个重物，移动就变慢且不情愿，即第二个义项。

branches.en: TIME: an event pulled beyond its length becomes both a drag on and a drag.
branches.cn: 时间线：被拉得过长的事件，既说 drag on，也成了 a drag，即第三、四个义项。

branches.en: PHYSICS: moving through air or water is held back as if pulled backwards.
branches.cn: 物理线：在空气或水中前进被向后拽住，即第五个义项。

branches.en: A dragged object and aerodynamic drag both describe opposing force.
branches.cn: 被拖的物体与气动阻力，都在描述一种对抗的力量。

intro.en: Drag is a Germanic word that accepts English endings and compounds easily.
intro.cn: drag 是日耳曼语词，很容易接英语词尾与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the root belongs to the Germanic family with draw.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先；这个词根与 draw 同属日耳曼语族。

items.example: The old verb underlies both draw and drag.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老动词同时支撑 draw 与 drag。

items.example: It forms dragged after doubling the g.
items.exampleCN: 双写 g 之后它构成 dragged。

items.meaning: a thing or person that does

derivatives.zh: 由 drag 加 -ing 构成，义为「拖沓的；令人疲惫的」
由 drag 加 net 复合，义为「拖网；大搜捕」

definition_zh: 龙；凶恶的人；蜥蜴类；严厉的女监护人
definition_en: a large mythical beast that breathes fire, or a fierce and frightening person
core_image: 鳞片覆身、张口喷火的巨兽伏在山口
scene: 古庙门前雕着一条盘绕的长兽，鳞片在香火里泛红。The carved dragon guards the temple gate.
sceneCN: 这里 dragon 是「龙」（第 1 个义项）；句意是那条雕刻的龙守着庙门。

pos.zh: 名词：龙；凶恶的人；蜥蜴类

derivatives.zh: 由 dragon 加 fly 复合而成，义为「蜻蜓」
由 dragon 加 -ish 构成，义为「像龙的；凶猛的」

senses.title: A fire-breathing mythical beast
senses.definition: a large imaginary animal in stories, often with wings, claws and fiery breath
senses.definitionCN: 传说中大型的想象动物，常有翅膀、利爪与喷火的能力
senses.example: The story ends with the knight killing a dragon.
senses.exampleCN: 故事以骑士杀死一条龙告终。
senses.why: Greek drakon first named a huge staring serpent, and that staring, gleaming creature is the ancestor of the modern dragon.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 drakon 最初指一条巨大、目光炯炯的蛇，正是那种瞪视、鳞光闪闪的形象成了今天「龙」的祖先。

senses.title: A fierce or cruel person
senses.definition: a person who is very fierce, strict, or frightening
senses.definitionCN: 非常凶悍、严厉或令人害怕的人
senses.example: Our new manager is a real dragon about deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新经理在截止日期上凶得厉害。
senses.why: Because the beast is fearsome, calling a person a dragon transfers the same menace onto them.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种兽令人生畏，把人称作 dragon，就是把同样的凶气转移到那个人身上。

senses.title: A small tropical lizard
senses.definition: a small lizard of warm regions, often with a fold of skin at the throat
senses.definitionCN: 产于温暖地区的小型蜥蜴，喉部常有皮褶
senses.example: A green dragon basked on the warm rock.
senses.exampleCN: 一只绿色的蜥蜴在温热的岩石上晒太阳。
senses.why: Small scaly reptiles look like miniature versions of the mythical beast, so biologists reused the name.
senses.whyCN: 披鳞的小爬行动物像是传说巨兽的缩小版，于是生物学家复用了这个名字。

senses.title: The Chinese imperial emblem
senses.definition: the long serpentine creature of Chinese art, a symbol of power and good fortune
senses.definitionCN: 中国艺术中修长的蛇形神兽，象征权力与吉祥
senses.example: The dragon on the robe marked the emperor alone.
senses.exampleCN: 袍上的龙纹只属于皇帝。
senses.why: When the Western word met Chinese art, the same name was given to a very different, auspicious creature.
senses.whyCN: 当西方的这个词遇到中国艺术，同一个名称被安到了一种截然不同、象征祥瑞的动物身上。

intro.en: Dragon came through Latin and French from Greek drakon, a huge serpent, and the word has always implied a stare.
intro.cn: dragon 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语 drakon，意为巨蛇，这个词从一开始就含「瞪视」的意味。

items.en: Drakon meant a large serpent, and it is usually linked to a verb meaning to look sharply or flash.
items.cn: drakon 意为巨蛇，一般认为它与表示「锐利地看、闪动」的动词有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as draco and used it for serpents and for a military standard.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 draco，用来指蛇类，也指一种军旗。

items.en: Old French passed the word into the shape that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传成英语借入时的形态。

items.en: English dragon first appears in religious and monster stories; the exact earliest text is debated.
items.cn: 英语 dragon 最早出现在宗教与怪物故事里；最早的文本究竟是哪一篇仍有争议。

items.en: The name spread to fierce people, to small lizards, and to the auspicious beast of Chinese art.
items.cn: 这个名字扩散到凶悍的人、小型蜥蜴，以及中国艺术中象征祥瑞的神兽。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on dragon or its Greek source; the near-meaning group gathers mythical creatures.
note.cn: 形近组建在 dragon 或其希腊语源头之上；近义组收的是其他神话生物。

entries.definition: The Latin form of the word, used for serpents and a constellation.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语形式，指蛇类，也是天龙座的名称。

entries.definition: A long-bodied flying insect with large transparent wings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜻蜓」，由 dragon 与 fly 复合而成。

entries.definition: Resembling a dragon; fierce.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「像龙的；凶猛的」，由 dragon 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: A large snake, often in myths and older stories.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巨蛇」，是 dragon 在希腊语时期的近邻概念。

entries.definition: A large or dangerous animal, real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「野兽」，可指真实或想象的凶猛动物。

entries.definition: A mythical creature with wings and two legs, distinct from a four-legged dragon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双足飞龙」，是龙类传说中的一个分支，与四足龙有别。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Greek staring serpent and the modern reuse of the name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着希腊语「瞪视的巨蛇」，以及这个名称的现代复用展开。

normal.en: Drakon meant a serpent that stares, and its glare survives in the modern beast.
normal.cn: drakon 指瞪视的巨蛇，那股瞪人的气势一直留在今天的龙形象里。

normal.en: Dragonfly keeps the beast's name on a harmless insect.
normal.cn: dragonfly 把这头巨兽的名字安在一种无害的昆虫上。

normal.en: Calling a strict manager a dragon borrows the beast's temper.
normal.cn: 把严厉的经理称作 dragon，是借用了这头兽的脾气。

normal.en: The Chinese dragon is a long serpent of good fortune, not a fire-breather.
normal.cn: 中国的龙是象征吉祥的长蛇形神兽，而不是喷火的怪兽。

normal.en: The dragon boat race keeps the name in celebration rather than fear.
normal.cn: 龙舟赛让这个名字从恐惧转向庆典。

abstract.en: Picture a carved beast coiled around a temple gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一头雕刻的巨兽盘绕在庙门旁。

abstract.en: Picture a shining eye opening in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一只发亮的眼睛睁开。

abstract.en: Picture a lizard on a hot stone suddenly looking huge.
abstract.cn: 想象石上晒太阳的蜥蜴忽然看起来变得巨大。

examples.en: In the tale, the dragon guards a cave of gold.
examples.cn: 故事里，那条龙守着一洞黄金。

examples.en: She can be a dragon when the rules are broken.
examples.cn: 一旦有人违规，她就会变得很凶。

examples.en: Dragon boat races fill the river every summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，龙舟赛让整条河热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓根」——传说中龙用爪子抓地，重新扎根，一看到就想起这条巨兽。

root: 经拉丁语 draco 与古法语来自希腊语 drakon（巨蛇）。drakon 一般认为与表示「锐利地看、闪动」的词有关，因为巨蛇的形象核心是瞪视与鳞光。英语借入后既指传说巨兽，也引申指凶悍的人、小型蜥蜴，并被挪用于中国艺术中的祥瑞神兽。

sensesIntro.en: One staring serpent in myth becomes a monster, a fierce person, a small lizard and an auspicious emblem.
sensesIntro.cn: 神话里一条瞪视的巨蛇，变成了怪兽、凶人、小蜥蜴与祥瑞纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scaled beast coiled at a gate with burning eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头鳞甲巨兽盘在门边，眼睛发亮。

branches.en: MONSTER: the first sense is the mythical beast of story and art.
branches.cn: 怪兽线：第一个义项是故事与艺术中的传说巨兽。

branches.en: PERSON: the beast's temper transfers to a fierce human being.
branches.cn: 人物线：巨兽的脾气被转移到凶悍的人身上，即第二个义项。

branches.en: LIZARD: small scaly reptiles borrow the ancient name.
branches.cn: 爬行线：披鳞的小爬行动物借用了这个古老名称，即第三个义项。

branches.en: CHINESE ART: the name was reused for a long, auspicious serpent.
branches.cn: 东方线：这个名字又被挪用于修长、象征祥瑞的神兽，即第四个义项。

branches.en: The monster and the fierce person share exactly the same menace.
branches.cn: 怪兽与凶人，共享同一种令人畏惧的气场。

intro.en: Dragon is a whole borrowed word, but English freely builds compounds and derived forms on it.
intro.cn: dragon 是整体借来的词，但英语仍能自由地用它造复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin draco is recorded, and Greek drakon stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 draco 有文献记录，其背后是希腊语 drakon。

items.example: The Greek noun is the earliest source.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是最早的来源。

items.example: Latin carried the word to Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带到欧洲。

derivatives.zh: 由 dragon 加 fly 复合，义为「蜻蜓」
由 dragon 加 -ish 构成，义为「像龙的」

definition_zh: 排水；流干；排水沟；下水道；耗尽；流失
definition_en: to make liquid flow away, or a pipe or channel that carries waste water away
core_image: 水池底部的旋涡，把所有水都吸下去
scene: 厨房水槽堵了，脏水漫过池沿，地面一片湿滑。He had to drain the sink before fixing the pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 drain 是「把水排掉」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他得先把水槽里的水排掉才能修管道。

pos.zh: 名词：排水沟；下水道；消耗

derivatives.zh: 由 drain 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「排水系统；排水」
由 drain 加 pipe 复合而成，义为「排水管」
由 drain 加 -ed 构成，义为「筋疲力尽的」

senses.title: To make liquid flow away
senses.definition: to remove water or another liquid from something by letting it flow out
senses.definitionCN: 让水或其他液体流出去，从而把它从某物中清除
senses.example: Drain the rice and leave it to cool.
senses.exampleCN: 把米沥干，放凉。
senses.why: The word descends from a Germanic root meaning to make dry, so its first job is simply to take liquid away.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「使干」的日耳曼词根，所以它最初的工作就是把液体带走。

senses.title: To flow away gradually
senses.definition: to flow out slowly until little or nothing is left
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢流出去，直到所剩无几
senses.example: The flood water drained away overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水一夜之间退去了。
senses.why: When the object is the liquid itself rather than a container, the same action becomes an intransitive flowing away.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是液体本身而不是容器时，同一个动作就变成不及物的「流走」。

senses.title: A channel that carries waste water
senses.definition: a pipe or open channel that carries away waste water or rainwater
senses.definitionCN: 把污水或雨水送走的管道或明沟
senses.example: Leaves blocked the drain outside the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶堵住了门外的排水沟。
senses.why: The thing that performs the draining takes the action's name, so the channel itself is called a drain.
senses.whyCN: 执行「排」这个动作的装置沿用了动作的名称，于是排水沟本身也叫 drain。

senses.title: To use up strength or money
senses.definition: to take away someone's energy, money, or resources until little is left
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的精力、金钱或资源抽走，直到所剩无几
senses.example: The long illness drained the family's savings.
senses.exampleCN: 这场漫长的病耗尽了家里的积蓄。
senses.why: Energy and money behave like liquid in this metaphor: they can be drawn out until the container is empty.
senses.whyCN: 在这个比喻里，精力与金钱就像液体，可以被抽走，直到容器见底。

senses.title: A steady loss of something valuable
senses.definition: a continuous loss of people, skills, or money from a place or system
senses.definitionCN: 人员、技能或资金从一个地方或体系中持续流失
