senses.example: The countryside suffers from a steady drain of young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村正承受年轻劳动力持续外流的压力。
senses.why: If draining empties a container drop by drop, the noun also names that slow emptying of a whole region.
senses.whyCN: 如果排水是一滴一滴把容器放空，那么这个名词也指一整个地区被慢慢抽空的过程。

intro.en: Drain comes from Old English drehnian, to strain or draw off liquid, and its family is Germanic.
intro.cn: drain 来自古英语 drehnian，意为「滤出、抽走液体」，其词族属日耳曼语。

items.en: A root meaning to make dry or to strain lies behind the English word; the exact shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: 英语这个词背后有一个表示「使干、过滤」的词根，其确切形态是重构出来的。

items.en: Drehnian meant to strain liquid off or to draw it away.
items.cn: drehnian 意为把液体滤出或抽走。

items.en: The verb settled as drayne and extended from kitchens to fields and mines.
items.cn: 动词固定为 drayne，并从厨房扩展到田地与矿井。

items.en: The noun appeared for the channel that carries water away; the earliest examples are roughly dated.
items.cn: 名词出现，指把水送走的沟渠；最早用例的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: The liquid image spread to energy, savings, and the loss of skilled people from a region.
items.cn: 液体的意象扩展到精力、积蓄，以及一个地区技术人才的外流。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates removing liquid from using it up.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把「排出液体」与「耗光」分开。

entries.definition: The system or process by which water is carried away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排水；排水系统」，由 drain 加 -age 构成。

entries.definition: A pipe that carries waste water away from a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排水管」，由 drain 与 pipe 复合。

entries.definition: Extremely tired, as if emptied of energy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「筋疲力尽的」，字面是「被抽空了」。

entries.definition: To remove everything from a container, not only liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「清空」，对象不限于液体。

entries.definition: To use something up completely, especially resources or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「耗尽」，多用于资源与精力。

entries.definition: An underground pipe for waste water and sewage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下水道」，规模比 drain 更大、更专门。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the liquid image from the sink to the region losing its workers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着液体的意象，从水槽一路走到人才外流的地区。

normal.en: Drain and dry share a meaning, so the word is about removing wetness.
normal.cn: drain 与 dry 意义相通，这个词的核心就是「去湿」。

normal.en: A drain is simply the thing that does the draining.
normal.cn: drain 这个装置，就是执行「排」这个动作的东西。

normal.en: Energy drains like water, which is why tired people feel drained.
normal.cn: 精力像水一样流走，所以累坏的人会觉得被抽空了。

normal.en: Brain drain means the cleverest people flow out of a country.
normal.cn: brain drain 指最聪明的人像水一样流出国外。

normal.en: A drain on resources is a slow leak you keep paying for.
normal.cn: a drain on resources 就是一处你不断为之付钱的慢性漏水。

abstract.en: Picture a whirlpool above a plug hole.
abstract.cn: 想象排水口上方转起的旋涡。

abstract.en: Picture a bathtub slowly emptying after the plug is pulled.
abstract.cn: 想象拔掉塞子后浴缸慢慢见底。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass whose sand will not stop falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙漏，沙子怎么也停不下来。

examples.en: Please drain the pasta before you add the sauce.
examples.cn: 加酱之前请先把面里的水沥干。

examples.en: The drain in the yard is blocked again.
examples.cn: 院子里的排水沟又堵了。

examples.en: Endless paperwork drained her energy.
examples.cn: 没完没了的文书工作耗尽了她的精力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽阴」——把水往阴沟里拽，drain 就是「排水、流走」。

root: 来自古英语 drehnian（滤出、抽走液体），属日耳曼语词族，与表示「使干」的词根相关。由「排掉液体」引申为「流走」、「排水沟」，再由液体的流失引申为精力、金钱的耗尽与人才外流。

sensesIntro.en: A single image of water leaving a container grows into pipes, exhaustion, and regional loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 「水离开容器」这一个画面，长出了管道、疲惫与地区性流失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whirlpool pulling every drop down a plug hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋涡把每一滴水都吸进排水口。

branches.en: WATER: the verb works both on the container and on the liquid itself.
branches.cn: 水线：这个动词既能作用在容器上，也能作用在液体本身上，即第一、二个义项。

branches.en: THE PIPE: the device that drains takes the action's name.
branches.cn: 管道线：执行排水动作的装置沿用了动作之名，即第三个义项。

branches.en: THE BODY: strength and money can be poured out like water.
branches.cn: 身体线：体力与金钱可以像水一样被倒空，即第四个义项。

branches.en: THE REGION: a place slowly empties of its skilled people.
branches.cn: 地区线：一个地方慢慢被抽走它的技术人才，即第五个义项。

branches.en: Draining a sink and draining a person share the same emptying motion.
branches.cn: 把水槽排空与把人耗空，共享同一个「倒空」的动作。

intro.en: Drain is a whole Germanic verb that also takes English endings and compounds.
intro.cn: drain 是完整的日耳曼语动词，同时能接英语词尾并参与复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; drainage uses a French-derived suffix that itself goes back to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身没有拉丁成分；drainage 用的 -age 后缀经法语转来，再往上才是拉丁语。

items.example: The old verb is the source of drain.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词是 drain 的来源。

items.example: Pulling the plug lets the water drain.

derivatives.zh: 由 drain 加 -age 构成，义为「排水；排水系统」
由 drain 与 pipe 复合，义为「排水管」

definition_zh: 戏剧；剧本；戏剧性事件；戏剧艺术
definition_en: a play written for the stage, or an exciting and emotional situation
core_image: 舞台上一束追光，把人的一举一动放大
scene: 剧场里灯光渐暗，幕布缓缓拉开，观众屏住呼吸。She studied drama at a small college in the north.
sceneCN: 这里 drama 是「戏剧（学科、艺术形式）」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她在北方一所小学校学习戏剧。

pos.zh: 名词：戏剧；剧本；戏剧性事件

derivatives.zh: 由 drama 加形容词后缀 -tic 构成，义为「戏剧的；戏剧性的」
由 drama 加表示「从事者」的 -tist 构成，义为「剧作家」
由 drama 加动词后缀 -tize 构成，义为「改编成剧本；夸大」

senses.title: The art of writing and performing plays
senses.definition: the art form of plays, or the study of writing and performing them
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧这一艺术形式，或对编剧与表演的学习
senses.example: He teaches drama at a secondary school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所中学教戏剧。
senses.why: Greek drama meant a deed or an action performed, so the art form is named after things being done on stage.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 drama 意为「被做的事、行动」，所以这种艺术形式是以「舞台上被做出来的事」命名的。

senses.title: A play or a serious television story
senses.definition: a single play, or a serious story broadcast on television
senses.definitionCN: 一部戏剧作品，或电视上播出的严肃故事
senses.example: The new drama about village life won several awards.
senses.exampleCN: 那部关于乡村生活的新剧拿了好几个奖。
senses.why: One performed action becomes a countable work, so a single play is also called a drama.
senses.whyCN: 一次被演出的行动变成一个可数的作品，所以单部戏也叫 drama。

senses.title: An exciting or tense situation
senses.definition: a situation full of emotion, conflict, or unexpected events
senses.definitionCN: 充满情绪、冲突或意外事件的局面
senses.example: There was some drama at the airport when the flight was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 航班取消时，机场里上演了一出闹剧。
senses.why: Real life that looks like a staged action borrows the stage word, so any tense scene becomes drama.
senses.whyCN: 现实生活一旦看起来像被搬上舞台的行动，就借用了舞台的词，于是任何紧张场面都叫 drama。

intro.en: Drama is a direct borrowing from Greek drama, a deed or an action, through Latin and French.
intro.cn: drama 直接借自希腊语 drama（行为、行动），经拉丁语与法语传入英语。

items.en: The verb dran meant to do or to act, and drama was the thing done.
items.cn: 动词 dran 意为「做、行动」，drama 就是「被做出来的事」。

items.en: In Athens drama named a staged action, and by extension a play for the theatre.
items.cn: 在雅典，drama 指被搬上舞台的行动，进而指供剧场演出的戏。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word for plays, keeping the theatrical sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个词指戏剧，保留了剧场含义。

items.en: English took the word from Latin and French; the earliest English examples date from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语与法语借入；最早的英语用例出现在十六世纪。

items.en: The word widened from stage works to television plays and then to any tense real event.
items.cn: 这个词从舞台作品扩展到电视剧，再扩展到任何紧张的真实事件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek root; the near-meaning group gathers related performance words.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊词根；近义组收的是相关的表演类词汇。

entries.definition: Relating to drama, or sudden and striking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「戏剧的；戏剧性的」，由 drama 加 -tic 构成。

entries.definition: A person who writes plays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剧作家」，由 drama 加 -tist 构成。

entries.definition: To turn a story into a play, or to make it seem more exciting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改编成剧；夸大渲染」，由 drama 加 -tize 构成。

entries.definition: A story performed by actors on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏剧、剧本」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The building for plays, or the art form as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剧院；戏剧（整体）」，偏重场所与门类。

entries.definition: A serious play with a sad ending.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「悲剧」，是 drama 的一个具体类型。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the Greek sense of a thing done and follow the word onto television and into daily life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从希腊语「被做的事」出发，跟着这个词走上电视、走进日常。

normal.en: Dran means to act, so drama is literally the acting.
normal.cn: dran 意为「行动」，所以 drama 字面就是「被演出来的行动」。

normal.en: Dramatic keeps the stage feeling, which is why a dramatic entrance turns heads.
normal.cn: dramatic 保留了舞台感，所以「戏剧性的登场」会让人回头。

normal.en: A dramatist is the person who makes the action happen on paper.
normal.cn: dramatist 就是在纸上让这些行动发生的人。

normal.en: To dramatize a novel is to turn reading into watching.
normal.cn: 把小说 dramatize，就是把「读」变成「看」。

normal.en: When people say there was drama, they mean real life copied the stage.
normal.cn: 人们说「发生了一出戏」，意思是现实生活照搬了舞台。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight cutting through a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一束追光切进漆黑的大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain rising inch by inch.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布一寸一寸升起。

abstract.en: Picture an audience holding its breath at once.
abstract.cn: 想象满场观众同时屏住呼吸。

examples.en: She has written three radio dramas this year.
examples.cn: 今年她写了三部广播剧。

examples.en: The drama department is putting on a Greek play.
examples.cn: 戏剧系正在排演一出希腊戏。

examples.en: There was a lot of drama before the vote was finally held.
examples.cn: 投票最终举行之前闹出了不少波折。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓马」——舞台上情节一抓一大把，抓马就是戏多，drama 正是「戏剧、戏多」。

root: 直接借自希腊语 drama（行为、被做的事），源自动词 dran（做、行动），经拉丁语与法语进入英语。因为戏剧就是「把行动演出来」，这个词天然带着「动作、冲突」的意味，后来引申为戏剧性事件。

sensesIntro.en: A performed action becomes an art form, then a countable play, then any tense real scene.
sensesIntro.cn: 被演出的行动先成为艺术门类，再成为可数的作品，最后成为任何紧张的真实场面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight that enlarges every gesture on stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束把所有动作都放大的舞台追光。

branches.en: ART: the first sense is the whole craft and its study.
branches.cn: 艺术线：第一个义项是这门技艺及其学科。

branches.en: WORK: a single play or television story is one acting-out of the craft.
branches.cn: 作品线：单部戏或电视剧是这门技艺的一次具体演出，即第二个义项。

branches.en: LIFE: a tense real event borrows the stage word for its own scenes.
branches.cn: 生活线：紧张的真实事件借用了舞台词来描述自己的场面，即第三个义项。

branches.en: The art form and the individual play are the class and its members.
branches.cn: 艺术门类与单部作品，是类别与其成员的关系。

branches.en: A television drama and a dramatic real event both hold an audience's attention.
branches.cn: 电视剧与戏剧性的真实事件，都能牢牢抓住观众的注意力。

intro.en: Drama is a borrowed stem that takes several Greek-derived English endings.
intro.cn: drama 是借来的词干，能接几个经希腊语而来的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin drama is recorded, but the word is originally Greek and reached English through French as well.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 drama 有记录，但这个词原本是希腊语，也经法语传入英语。

items.example: The verb is the root of drama.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 drama 的词根。
这个名词原样进入英语。

items.example: Theatre names the building and the field.

derivatives.zh: 由 drama 加 -tic 构成，义为「戏剧的；戏剧性的」
由 drama 加 -tist 构成，义为「剧作家」

definition_zh: 戏剧的；戏剧性的；显著的；夸张的
definition_en: relating to drama, or sudden, striking, and full of strong feeling
core_image: 门被推开的一瞬，所有目光都转过去
scene: 会场忽然安静，灯光一转，演讲者从侧门大步走上台。The announcement had a dramatic effect on the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 dramatic 是「显著的、戏剧性的」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这项宣布对人群产生了显著的影响。

pos.zh: 形容词：戏剧的；戏剧性的；显著的；夸张的

derivatives.zh: 由 dramatic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「大幅度地；戏剧性地」
由 dramatic 加 -s 构成，义为「戏剧表演；夸张做作」

senses.title: Relating to plays and acting
senses.definition: connected with plays, acting, or the theatre
senses.definitionCN: 与戏剧、表演或剧院有关的
senses.example: She joined a dramatic society at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学加入了一个戏剧社。
senses.why: The Greek noun drama named a staged action, and the ending -tic simply means belonging to it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名词 drama 指被搬上舞台的行动，后缀 -tic 只表示「属于它」，所以这是最本分的义项。

senses.title: Sudden and very noticeable
senses.definition: large, sudden, and easy to notice, especially of a change or an effect
senses.definitionCN: 幅度大、来得突然、很容易被注意到，多形容变化或效果
senses.example: There has been a dramatic fall in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 价格出现了大幅下跌。
senses.why: A change that would look striking on stage is called dramatic, so the word came to mean strikingly large.
senses.whyCN: 一个在舞台上会显得触目惊心的变化，就被称作 dramatic，于是这个词有了「幅度惊人」的意思。

senses.title: Showy and full of strong feeling
senses.definition: expressing feelings in an exaggerated, theatrical way
senses.definitionCN: 以夸张、像演戏一样的方式表达情绪
senses.example: He let out a dramatic sigh and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸张地叹了口气，走出了房间。
senses.why: When ordinary behaviour copies stage acting, the same adjective describes it as overdone.
senses.whyCN: 当日常举动模仿舞台表演时，同一个形容词就用来形容它「演过头了」。

intro.en: Dramatic is Greek drama plus the adjective ending -tikos, filtered through Latin dramaticus and French dramatique.
intro.cn: dramatic 由希腊语 drama 加形容词词尾 -tikos 构成，经拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 传入英语。

items.en: Dran meant to do or act, and drama was the deed performed.
items.cn: dran 意为「做、行动」，drama 是被做出来的事。

items.en: The adjective meant skilled in acting or belonging to drama.
items.cn: 这个形容词表示「擅长表演的」或「属于戏剧的」。

items.en: Latin kept the adjective for anything connected with plays.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留这个形容词，指与戏剧有关的事物。

items.en: French carried the form toward modern spelling and meaning.
items.cn: 法语把这个形式推向近代拼写与含义。

items.en: English adopted dramatic for stage matters and soon extended it to striking events.
items.cn: 英语采用 dramatic 指舞台事务，很快又扩展到惊人的事件。

items.en: The word now covers theatre, big changes, and exaggerated behaviour.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖戏剧、巨大变化与夸张举止三方面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family; the near-meaning group compares three words for striking change.
note.cn: 形近组同属一个词族；近义组比较三个表示「变化惊人」的词。

entries.definition: A play, or the art of performing plays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏剧」，是 dramatic 的基础词。

entries.definition: In a striking way, or by a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大幅度地；戏剧性地」，由 dramatic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: To adapt for the stage or to exaggerate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改编成剧；夸大」，与 dramatic 同族。

entries.definition: Very noticeable and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人注目的」，强调视觉冲击。

entries.definition: Sudden and large, especially of a change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「急剧的」，多修饰变化的幅度。

entries.definition: Exaggerated in manner, like an actor on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「夸张做作的」，偏贬义，接近 dramatic 的第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the stage picture from real theatre to big changes to overacting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着舞台画面，从真正的戏剧走到巨大变化，再到演过头。

normal.en: Drama plus -tic simply means of the stage.
normal.cn: drama 加 -tic 就是「属于舞台的」。

normal.en: A dramatic rise is a change big enough to look like a scene.
normal.cn: dramatic rise 就是大到像一场戏的变化。

normal.en: Dramatic irony is the audience knowing what the character does not.
normal.cn: dramatic irony 指观众知道而剧中人不知道。

normal.en: A dramatic sigh is acting without a stage.
normal.cn: dramatic sigh 就是没有舞台的表演。

normal.en: Dramatics as a plural noun means either amateur theatre or showy behaviour.
normal.cn: 复数名词 dramatics 既指业余戏剧，也指做作的举止。

abstract.en: Picture a door thrown open and every head turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被推开，所有脑袋同时转过去。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line dropping off the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线陡降，几乎掉出纸外。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to the forehead in mock despair.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按上额头，装作绝望。

examples.en: The city has seen dramatic growth in ten years.
examples.cn: 这座城市十年间出现了惊人的增长。

examples.en: Her dramatic reading held the whole room.
examples.cn: 她富有戏剧感的朗诵镇住了全场。

examples.en: He made a dramatic gesture with his coat and left.
examples.cn: 他夸张地甩了一下外套就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: drama 是「戏」，-tic 是「……的」，所以 dramatic 是「像戏一样的」：既能指真的戏剧，也能指惊人的变化和夸张的举止。

root: 由希腊语 drama（行为、戏剧）加形容词词尾 -tikos 构成，经拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 进入英语。核心含义始终是「像舞台上那样引人注目」，因此兼指戏剧本身、巨大的变化与夸张的表达。

sensesIntro.en: From the stage the adjective moves to changes that look stage-worthy, then to people who act as if on stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从舞台出发，移向「像戏一样」的变化，再移向「仿佛在台上」的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door thrown open while every head turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被推开，所有目光同时转过去。

branches.en: THEATRE: the literal sense belongs to plays and acting.
branches.cn: 剧场线：字面义属于戏剧与表演，即第一个义项。

branches.en: SCALE: a change big enough to stage is described as dramatic.
branches.cn: 幅度线：大到可以搬上舞台的变化，被形容为 dramatic，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MANNER: behaviour that copies stage acting is called dramatic.
branches.cn: 举止线：模仿舞台表演的行为也叫 dramatic，即第三个义项。

branches.en: Real theatre and overacting share the same visible gestures.
branches.cn: 真正的戏剧与做作的举止，共享同一套夸张可见的手势。

branches.en: Both a dramatic fall and a dramatic sigh are meant to be noticed.
branches.cn: 大幅下跌与夸张的叹息，都是为了被人注意到。

intro.en: Dramatic is a Greek stem with a Greek adjective ending, reshaped by Latin and French.
intro.cn: dramatic 是希腊词干加希腊形容词词尾，再经拉丁语与法语改造的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin dramaticus is recorded, and the Greek ending -tikos appears in Latin as -ticus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dramaticus 有文献记录，希腊词尾 -tikos 在拉丁语中作 -ticus。

items.example: Drama is the stem of dramatic.
items.exampleCN: drama 是 dramatic 的词干。

items.meaningCN: 复数形式表示一门活动

items.meaning: a gap between appearance and reality

items.example: Dramatic effect is a common pairing.
Dramatic change is a common pairing.
Dramatic entrance is a common pairing.

derivatives.zh: 由 dramatic 加 -ally 构成，义为「大幅度地；戏剧性地」
由 dramatic 加 -s 构成，义为「戏剧表演；做作举止」

definition_zh: 大幅度地；显著地；戏剧性地；夸张地
definition_en: by a large and noticeable amount, or in a showy, theatrical way
core_image: 曲线突然折下去，像被人猛拽了一把
scene: 报告念到一半，会议室里的人同时抬头，因为屏幕上的数字几乎腰斩。Sales fell dramatically in the second quarter.
sceneCN: 这里 dramatically 是「大幅度地」（第 1 个义项）；句意是第二季度销量大幅下滑。

pos.zh: 副词：大幅度地；显著地；戏剧性地；夸张地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ally 的形式，义为「戏剧的；戏剧性的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 dramatically 构成，义为「不引人注目地」

senses.title: By a very large amount
senses.definition: to a degree that is large, sudden, and easy to notice
senses.definitionCN: 达到幅度大、来得突然、很容易被注意到的程度
senses.example: Prices have dropped dramatically since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 入春以来价格大幅下跌。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's sense of a change big enough to look like a stage scene, so it simply intensifies the size of the change.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词带着形容词「大到像一台戏」的含义，所以它只是把变化的幅度再推高一档。

senses.title: In a theatrical or striking way
senses.definition: in a way that is sudden, striking, or like a scene from a play
senses.definitionCN: 以突然、触目惊心、像戏中一场的方式
senses.example: The evening ended dramatically with a power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 那晚以一场停电戏剧性地收场。
senses.why: When an event unfolds like a staged scene, the adverb describes its manner rather than its size.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事像舞台上的一场戏那样展开时，这个副词描述的是它的方式，而不是幅度。

senses.title: In an exaggerated manner
senses.definition: in a showy way that draws attention to oneself
senses.definitionCN: 以招摇、引人注意的方式
senses.example: She sighed dramatically and closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她夸张地叹了口气，把门关上。
senses.why: If someone behaves as though an audience were watching, the adverb marks the overacting.
senses.whyCN: 如果有人表现得像有观众在看，这个副词就点出了那份「演过头」。

intro.en: Dramatically is dramatic plus -ally, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb.
intro.cn: dramatically 是 dramatic 加 -ally，即英语把形容词变成副词的一般方式。

items.en: Drama named a staged action, from the verb dran, to do.
items.cn: drama 指被搬上舞台的行动，源自动词 dran（做）。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to drama or skilled in acting.
items.cn: 这个形容词表示「属于戏剧的」或「擅长表演的」。

items.en: Latin dramaticus and French dramatique carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 把这个形容词送到英语。

items.en: Dramatic entered English; the adverb followed with the usual -ally ending.
items.cn: dramatic 进入英语，副词随后按常规加 -ally 形成。

items.en: The adverb became especially common with verbs of change such as rise, fall and improve.
items.cn: 这个副词尤其常与 rise、fall、improve 这类表示变化的动词连用。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same stem; the near-meaning group compares adverbs of degree.
note.cn: 形近组建在同一词干上；近义组比较几个程度副词。

entries.definition: Relating to drama, or suddenly striking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「戏剧的；戏剧性的」，是 dramatically 的基础形式。

entries.definition: A play, or the art of plays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏剧」，与 dramatically 同族。

entries.definition: To adapt for performance or to exaggerate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改编成剧；夸大」。

entries.definition: Suddenly and by a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「急剧地」，多用于数字与价格。

entries.definition: By an amount large enough to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「显著地」，强调重要性而非视觉冲击。

entries.definition: In an exaggerated, stage-like way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「夸张地、像演戏地」，偏贬义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the three directions of the adverb: size, style, and overacting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住这个副词的三个方向：幅度、风格与做作。

normal.en: Dramatic plus -ally keeps all three meanings of the adjective.
normal.cn: dramatic 加 -ally，完整保留了形容词的三层含义。

normal.en: With rise and fall it means by a lot, not like a play.
normal.cn: 和 rise、fall 连用时，它表示幅度大，而不是像演戏。

normal.en: With ended or arrived it often means like a scene from a play.
normal.cn: 和 ended、arrived 连用时，它多表示「像戏里的一场」。

normal.en: With sighed or waved it points at overacting.
normal.cn: 和 sighed、waved 连用时，它指的则是演过头。

normal.en: Sharply is its closest rival in economic writing.
normal.cn: 在经济类文章里，sharply 是它最接近的对手。

abstract.en: Picture a chart line falling off the bottom edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条图表线直接掉出下边缘。

abstract.en: Picture lights going out exactly at the climax.
abstract.cn: 想象高潮刚起，灯突然全灭。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flung to the forehead in front of an audience.
abstract.cn: 想象在观众面前，一只手夸张地甩上额头。

examples.en: The cost of solar panels has fallen dramatically.
examples.cn: 太阳能板的成本大幅下降。

examples.en: The trial ended dramatically when a new witness appeared.
examples.cn: 一名新证人出现，审判戏剧性地收场。

examples.en: He bowed dramatically before leaving the stage.
examples.cn: 他夸张地鞠了一躬才离开舞台。

dict_mnemonic.text: dramatic 是「戏剧性的」，加 -ally 变成副词：数字变化大就是「大幅度地」，举止像演戏就是「夸张地」。

root: 由 dramatic 加副词词尾 -ally 构成。dramatic 源自希腊语 drama（戏剧）加 -tikos，经拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 传入英语。因「戏剧性的」本身兼指「幅度惊人」与「像演戏」，副词也继承这两条线。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb keeps three faces of the adjective: sheer size, sudden style, and showy manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词保留了形容词的三张面孔：纯幅度、突如其来的风格，以及做作的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a chart dropping off the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上一条线陡直掉出纸外。

branches.en: DEGREE: before verbs of change, the adverb means by a lot.
branches.cn: 程度线：放在表示变化的动词前，它表示「幅度很大」，即第一个义项。

branches.en: STYLE: an event unfolding like a staged scene takes the same adverb.
branches.cn: 风格线：像舞台一场那样展开的事件，也用这个副词，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MANNER: visible overacting is marked by the same word.
branches.cn: 举止线：看得见的做作，同样用这个词标注，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A dramatic fall and a dramatic ending both demand attention.
branches.cn: 大幅下跌与戏剧性的收场，都在强求注意力。

branches.en: A scene-like event and an exaggerated sigh both look performed.
branches.cn: 像戏的事件与夸张的叹息，看起来都像被表演出来的。

intro.en: Dramatically is a straightforward adverb build on the adjective dramatic.
intro.cn: dramatically 是在形容词 dramatic 上直接构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek, the adjective ending came through Latin, and -ally is the English adverb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是希腊语，形容词词尾经拉丁语而来，-ally 则是英语的副词词尾。

items.example: The noun is the distant stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是最远的词干。

Fall dramatically is a common pairing.
Change dramatically is a common pairing.
Improve dramatically is a common pairing.
Sharply often replaces dramatically in data writing.
items.exampleCN: 在数据类写作中，sharply 常替代 dramatically。

definition_zh: 穿堂风；气流；一饮之量；生啤；吃水深度
definition_en: a current of cool air coming into a room, or a single swallow of a drink
core_image: 门缝下钻进的一股冷气，贴着地面爬
scene: 冬夜的屋里暖气很足，脚边却凉飕飕的，寒气从门底渗进来。A cold draught crept in under the door.
sceneCN: 这里 draught 是「穿堂风、气流」（第 1 个义项）；句意是一股冷风从门底下渗进来。

pos.zh: 名词：气流；一饮之量；生啤

derivatives.zh: 由 draught 加 -y 构成，义为「有穿堂风的、漏风的」
由 draught 加 man 复合而成，义为「制图员」

senses.title: A current of air in a room
senses.definition: a flow of cool air coming into a room through a window, door, or gap
senses.definitionCN: 通过窗户、门或缝隙进入房间的冷空气流
senses.example: She sat away from the window to avoid the draught.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐得离窗远些，以免被风吹着。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to draw or pull, and air literally gets pulled through a gap.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「拉、抽」的动词，风正是被从缝隙里抽进来的。

senses.title: The amount swallowed at one time
senses.definition: the quantity of liquid taken in a single swallow
senses.definitionCN: 一次吞下的液体量
senses.example: He emptied the glass in one draught.
senses.exampleCN: 他一口气把杯子喝空了。
senses.why: Liquid is also drawn down the throat in one pull, so the same word names a single swallow.
senses.whyCN: 液体也是一下被「抽」下喉咙的，所以同一个词又指「一口之量」。

senses.title: Beer served from a barrel
senses.definition: beer drawn from a large container rather than poured from a bottle
senses.definitionCN: 从大桶里打出来而不是从瓶里倒出的啤酒
senses.example: The pub serves draught beer from local breweries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒馆供应本地酒厂的生啤。
senses.why: Beer pulled from a cask is drawn out by a tap, so it takes the name of the drawing action.
senses.whyCN: 从酒桶里打出的啤酒是被龙头「抽」出来的，于是沿用了这个「抽取」动作的名字。

senses.title: The depth of water a boat needs
senses.definition: the depth of water needed for a ship to float without touching the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 船浮起时不触底所需的水深
senses.example: The harbour is too shallow for vessels of that draught.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口太浅，容不下吃水那么深的船。
senses.why: The loaded hull draws water down around it, so the depth it pulls is also called its draught.
senses.whyCN: 满载的船体把水在四周「拉」下去，于是它拉出的深度也叫吃水深度。

intro.en: Draught is the older British spelling of the same word that appears as draft in American English.
intro.cn: draught 是英式旧拼写，与美式英语里的 draft 是同一个词。

items.en: Dragan meant to draw or pull and is the ancestor of modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拉、拖」，是现代 draw 的祖先。

items.en: Draught named the act of drawing and then the thing drawn, including air pulled through a gap.
items.cn: draught 指「拉、抽」的动作，进而指被抽出的东西，包括穿过缝隙的空气。

items.en: The air sense is recorded from the medieval period; exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示气流的义项在中古时期已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The drink and beer senses developed from the idea of liquid drawn at one pull.
items.cn: 饮品与生啤义从「一口气抽下的液体」这个想法发展而来。

items.en: American English settled on draft for most senses, while British English kept draught for air and beer.
items.cn: 美式英语多数义项用 draft，英式英语则保留 draught 指气流与啤酒。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same word or its family; the near-meaning group names air and drink quantities.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个词或其词族；近义组收的是气流与饮量的说法。

entries.definition: The American spelling, used for air, beer, plans and conscription.
entries.definitionCN: 美式拼写，兼指气流、生啤、草稿与征兵，与 draught 同源。

entries.definition: To pull something toward you, or to sketch with lines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉；画」，是 draught 的远亲基础词。

entries.definition: Full of cold air currents.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漏风的」，由 draught 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A light gentle wind, usually outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微风」，多指室外，语气比 draught 温和。

entries.definition: A very small mouthful of a drink.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一小口」，量比 draught 少得多。

entries.definition: A large quick swallow of a drink.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一大口」，强调吞咽的动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the single pulling image behind air, beer and boat depth.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着「抽、拉」这一个意象，串起气流、啤酒与吃水。

normal.en: Draught and draft are one word with two spellings.
normal.cn: draught 与 draft 是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: Air is pulled through a gap, so a draught is always something coming in.
normal.cn: 空气是被抽进缝隙的，所以 draught 总是「进来的风」。

normal.en: Draught beer is pulled from a cask by a tap.
normal.cn: draught beer 是用龙头从酒桶里打出来的。

normal.en: In one draught copies the single pull of swallowing.
normal.cn: in one draught 照搬了「一口吞下」的那一次抽拉。

normal.en: A ship draws water around its hull, and the depth it draws is its draught.
normal.cn: 船把水在船体周围压低，压出的深度就是它的吃水。

abstract.en: Picture cold air crawling along a floor under a door.
abstract.cn: 想象冷空气贴着地面从门底下爬进来。

abstract.en: Picture a glass being emptied in one motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯酒被一个动作喝干。

abstract.en: Picture a hull pressing a dent into the water.
abstract.cn: 想象船体在水面上压出一道凹陷。

examples.en: Could you close the window? There is a draught.
examples.cn: 能把窗户关上吗？有风。

examples.en: They serve draught beer in the back room.
examples.cn: 他们在后屋供应生啤。

examples.en: The ferry has a shallow draught and can enter small ports.
examples.cn: 这艘渡船吃水浅，能进入小港口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓夫特」——风从门缝被抓进来，就是穿堂风；啤酒从桶里被抓出来，就是生啤。

root: 与 draft 同源，来自中古英语 draught（拉、抽），再追溯至古英语 dragan（拉、拖、画）。由「抽进来的空气」得气流义，由「一口抽下的液体」得饮量与生啤义，由「船体压低水面」得吃水义。

sensesIntro.en: One pulling action supplies four senses: air drawn in, a swallow, beer tapped from a barrel, and water drawn down by a hull.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抽拉」动作给出四个义项：抽进来的空气、一口饮下、从桶里打出的啤酒，以及船体压低的水深。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cold air crawling under a door along the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷气贴着地面从门缝钻进来。

branches.en: AIR: the most familiar sense is cold air entering a room.
branches.cn: 气流线：最熟悉的义项是进入房间的冷空气，即第一个义项。

branches.en: DRINK: one pull at the throat measures a single swallow.
branches.cn: 饮量线：喉咙的一次抽拉量出一口之量，即第二个义项。

branches.en: BEER: drink pulled from a cask by a tap keeps the action's name.
branches.cn: 啤酒线：用龙头从桶里打出的酒沿用了动作之名，即第三个义项。

branches.en: SHIPS: a hull draws water down, and the depth it draws is named after it.
branches.cn: 船舶线：船体把水压低，压出的深度由此得名，即第四个义项。

branches.en: A cold draught and a draught of beer both describe something being pulled toward you.
branches.cn: 冷风与一杯生啤，都在描述某物被抽向你的过程。

intro.en: Draught is a whole Germanic word that still accepts ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: draught 是完整的日耳曼语词，仍可接普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is involved; the root is the same one that produced draw.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先；这个词根也生出了 draw。

items.example: The old verb is the ancestor of draught.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词是 draught 的祖先。

items.example: Draw and draught share one root.
items.exampleCN: draw 与 draught 共享一个词根。

items.example: A tap pulls draught beer from the cask.
items.exampleCN: 龙头把生啤从酒桶里打出来。

items.example: Draught beer comes from a cask.

derivatives.zh: 由 draught 加 -y 构成，义为「漏风的」

definition_zh: 画；拉；抽；吸引；提取；平局；抽签
definition_en: to make a picture with lines, to pull something, or to attract attention
core_image: 一支笔在纸上划出第一道线
scene: 孩子坐在窗边，把外面的树一棵棵画进本子里。He sat by the window and began to draw the trees outside.
sceneCN: 这里 draw 是「画」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他坐在窗边开始画外面的树。

pos.zh: 名词：平局；抽签；吸引人的事物

derivatives.zh: 由 draw 加 -ing 构成，义为「图画；绘画」
由 draw 加 -er 构成，义为「抽屉；开票人」
由 draw 加 back 复合而成，义为「缺点；不利之处」
由前缀 with-（回去）加 draw 构成，义为「撤回；取款」

senses.title: To make a picture with lines
senses.definition: to make a picture or diagram with a pen or pencil
senses.definitionCN: 用笔画出一幅图或示意图
senses.example: She drew a map on the back of an envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 她在信封背面画了一张地图。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to drag a pen across a surface, and the line left behind turns the pulling motion into a picture.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是拖着一支笔划过纸面，留下的线条就把「拖」这个动作变成了一幅画。

senses.title: To pull something toward you
senses.definition: to pull something such as a curtain or a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 拉动窗帘、武器等物体
senses.example: He drew the curtains before turning on the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 他开灯前先把窗帘拉上。
senses.why: This is the literal pulling action that the whole family of words grew from.
senses.whyCN: 这就是整个词族赖以生长的那个字面动作：用力往回拉。

senses.title: To attract interest or attention
senses.definition: to cause people to look, come, or feel interested
senses.definitionCN: 使人过来、注视或产生兴趣
senses.example: The exhibition drew large crowds all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天这个展览吸引了大批观众。
senses.why: People are pulled toward what interests them, so attracting a crowd uses the same pulling verb.
senses.whyCN: 人会被感兴趣的东西「拉」过去，所以吸引人群用的还是同一个「拉」的动词。

senses.title: To take money out of an account
senses.definition: to take money from a bank account or to receive a salary
senses.definitionCN: 从银行账户里取出钱，或领取薪水
senses.example: I need to draw some cash before the shops close.
senses.exampleCN: 我得在商店关门前取点现金。
senses.why: Money is pulled out of an account just as water is pulled from a well, so the verb covers withdrawals.
senses.whyCN: 钱是从账户里被「拉」出来的，就像水从井里被抽出来，所以这个词也覆盖取款。

senses.title: To reach a result after thinking
senses.definition: to form an opinion or conclusion after considering facts
senses.definitionCN: 在考虑事实后形成看法或结论
senses.example: We can draw a clear conclusion from these figures.
senses.exampleCN: 从这些数字里我们可以得出一个清楚的结论。
senses.why: A conclusion is pulled out of scattered facts the way water is drawn from a well, hence the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 结论是从零散事实里被「抽」出来的，正如水从井里被抽出，所以用同一个动词。

senses.title: To end a game with equal scores
senses.definition: to finish a game or match with the same score for both sides
senses.definitionCN: 比赛结束时双方得分相同
senses.example: The two teams drew one all.
senses.exampleCN: 两队一比一战平。
senses.why: When neither side can pull ahead, the contest is level, and the noun draw names that level result.
senses.whyCN: 当任何一方都拉不开差距时，比赛就打平了，名词 draw 正指这个持平的结果。

senses.title: To choose by picking lots
senses.definition: to select someone or something by taking a card or a lot at random
senses.definitionCN: 通过随机抽取签或卡片来选出人或物
senses.example: They drew the names from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从帽子里抽出名字。
senses.why: A slip is literally pulled out of a container, so random selection is also called drawing.
senses.whyCN: 签是从容器里被实实在在地抽出来的，所以随机抽取也叫 drawing。

intro.en: Draw goes back to Old English dragan, to drag or pull, and the writing sense grew from dragging a pen.
intro.cn: draw 可追溯到古英语 dragan（拖、拉），「画」的义项就来自拖笔的动作。

items.en: The pulling root behind draw is usually reconstructed with the sense of dragging; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: draw 背后的「拉」词根一般被重构为带「拖」义的形式，确切形态不确定。

items.en: Dragan meant to drag or pull, and it also covered drawing a line across a surface.
items.cn: dragan 意为「拖、拉」，也涵盖在表面上拖出一道线。

items.en: The past forms drew and drawn settled, and the picture sense became central.
items.cn: 过去式 drew 与过去分词 drawn 固定下来，「画」的义项成为中心。

items.en: The verb extended to pulling money, attracting people and reaching conclusions.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到取钱、吸引人与得出结论。

items.en: The noun draw appeared for a tied game and for a random selection.
items.cn: 名词 draw 出现，指平局与随机抽取。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem or the root; the near-meaning group separates sketching from pulling.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干或词根；近义组把「素描」与「拉」分开。

entries.definition: A picture made with lines, or the activity of making one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图画；绘画」，由 draw 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A box that slides out of furniture; the pronunciation differs from draw.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抽屉」，由 draw 加 -er 构成，注意读音与 draw 不同。

entries.definition: To take back or remove, especially money or troops.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤回；取款」，由 with- 加 draw 构成。

entries.definition: A disadvantage that holds you back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点」，字面是「往后拉的东西」。

entries.definition: To draw quickly and roughly, without detail.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「速写」，强调快速粗略。

entries.definition: To move something toward you with force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拉」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: To cause people or things to come closer.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸引」，与 draw 的第三个义项接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the drag of a pen and the pulls that produced money, crowds and conclusions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着拖笔的动作，以及由此产生的取钱、聚人、得结论三条线展开。

normal.en: Dragan meant to drag, and a pen dragged across paper leaves a picture.
normal.cn: dragan 意为「拖」，笔在纸上拖过就留下了一幅画。

normal.en: The past forms are drew and drawn, not drawed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 drew，过去分词是 drawn，不是 drawed。

normal.en: Money is drawn out of a bank the way water is drawn from a well.
normal.cn: 钱从银行被取出，就像水从井里被抽出。

normal.en: A crowd is drawn to a good exhibition, pulled by interest.
normal.cn: 人群被好展览吸引过去，是被兴趣拉过去的。

normal.en: A draw keeps both sides level, because neither could pull ahead.
normal.cn: 平局意味着双方持平，因为谁都拉不开差距。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil leaving its first line on blank paper.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔在空白纸面上留下第一道线。

abstract.en: Picture a rope being hauled out of deep water.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子从深水里被拉上来。

abstract.en: Picture two scoreboards frozen at the same number.
abstract.cn: 想象两块记分牌停在同一个数字上。

examples.en: The children drew animals on the pavement.
examples.cn: 孩子们在人行道上画动物。

examples.en: Her speech drew tears from half the room.
examples.cn: 她的演讲让半个会场的人都流了泪。

examples.en: The match ended in a draw after extra time.
examples.cn: 加时赛后比赛以平局收场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捉」——把视线、把人、把钱都捉过来，就是 draw 的「拉、吸引、取」；笔在纸上捉出一条线，就是「画」。

root: 来自古英语 dragan（拖、拉），与 drag、draught 同源，词根属日耳曼语。由「拖笔划过纸面」得绘画义，由「往回拉」得拉拽义，由「把人拉过来」得吸引义，由「从账户或容器中抽出」得取款、抽签、得结论诸义；比赛打平时双方拉不开差距，故名词 draw 兼指平局。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of draw is a version of one pull: a pen, a curtain, a crowd, money, a conclusion, a lottery slip, a level score.
sensesIntro.cn: draw 的每个义项都是同一次「拉」的变体：拉笔、拉窗帘、拉人群、拉钱、拉出结论、抽出签、拉平比分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen dragged across paper, leaving the first line.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔在纸面上拖出第一道线。

branches.en: ART: dragging a pen turns into drawing a picture.
branches.cn: 绘画线：拖笔的动作变成了画图，即第一个义项。

branches.en: PULLING: the literal sense keeps curtains and weapons in view.
branches.cn: 拉拽线：字面义保留在窗帘与武器这类对象上，即第二个义项。

branches.en: INWARD: crowds and money are both pulled toward a centre.
branches.cn: 向内线：人群与钱都是被拉向某个中心，即第三、四个义项。

branches.en: EXTRACTED: conclusions and lottery slips are drawn out of facts or a hat.
branches.cn: 抽取线：结论与签分别从事理和帽子里被抽出，即第五、七个义项。

branches.en: LEVEL: a draw happens when neither side can pull ahead.
branches.cn: 持平线：当双方都拉不开差距时就是平局，即第六个义项。

intro.en: Draw is a strong English verb with irregular forms and a large family of compounds.
intro.cn: draw 是强势的英语动词，形式不规则，复合词家族庞大。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin, though the prefix with- in withdraw comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；withdraw 里的 with- 也来自古英语。

items.example: The old verb is the source of draw.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词是 draw 的来源。

items.meaning: a thing or person that does

items.example: It forms draw up, as in a plan.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 draw up，如拟定计划。

derivatives.zh: 由 draw 加 -ing 构成，义为「图画；绘画」
由 with- 加 draw 构成，义为「撤回；取款」

definition_zh: 抽屉；开票人；制图者；内裤（复数 drawers）
definition_en: a box that slides in and out of a piece of furniture, or a person who draws
core_image: 拉开柜门，抽屉滑出来，露出里面的杂物
scene: 找钥匙的时候，她把柜子一层层拉开，最底下那层塞满了旧票据。The spare keys are in the top drawer.
sceneCN: 这里 drawer 是「抽屉」（第 1 个义项）；句意是备用钥匙在最上面那个抽屉里。

pos.zh: 名词：抽屉；开票人；制图者

collocations.phrase: not be out of the top drawer

derivatives.zh: drawer 的复数，另指「内裤」，属英式旧说法
由 drawer 加 -ful（满……的量）构成，义为「一抽屉之量」

senses.title: A sliding box in furniture
senses.definition: a container shaped like a box that slides in and out of a desk, cupboard, or chest
senses.definitionCN: 装在书桌、柜子或柜斗里、可推拉的箱形容器
senses.example: He kept his passport in the bottom drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他把护照放在最下面的抽屉里。
senses.why: The box is named after the action of drawing it out, so the drawer is literally the thing that is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这个箱子是以「被拉出来」这个动作命名的，抽屉正是那个被拉动的东西。

senses.title: A person who draws pictures or bills
senses.definition: a person who draws pictures, or one who writes an order for payment
senses.definitionCN: 绘制图画的人，或开出付款单据的人
senses.example: The drawer of the cheque must sign it.
senses.exampleCN: 支票的开票人必须签字。
senses.why: The -er ending marks the person doing the drawing, whether of lines or of a bill.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标示做这个动作的人，无论是画线条还是开票据。

intro.en: Drawer is draw plus -er, and its furniture sense grew from the sliding action of pulling a box out.
intro.cn: drawer 是 draw 加 -er 构成，家具义来自「把箱子拉出来」这个推拉动作。

items.en: Dragan meant to drag or pull and became modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拖、拉」，演变为现代的 draw。

items.en: The -er form first named a person who draws, whether pictures or documents.
items.cn: -er 形式最初指「画的人」，可以是画画的人，也可以是开单据的人。

items.en: The furniture sense appeared for a sliding box; the earliest records are roughly dated.
items.cn: 表示可推拉的箱子的义项出现，最早记录的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: Chest of drawers and top drawer became fixed household phrases.
items.cn: chest of drawers 与 top drawer 成为固定的家庭用语。

items.en: The pronunciation /drɔːr/ lost the w that is still heard in the verb draw.
items.cn: 读音 /drɔːr/ 丢掉了动词 draw 里仍能听到的那个 w。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the family and the spelling trap; the near-meaning group names furniture parts.
note.cn: 形近组展示这个词族与拼写陷阱；近义组收的是家具部件。

entries.definition: To sketch or pull; the verb kept its w in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「画；拉」，是 drawer 的基础词，读音保留 w。

entries.definition: The plural, also an old word for underpants.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，另可指旧式的「内裤」。

entries.definition: A picture made with lines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「图画」，与 drawer 同族。

entries.definition: A piece of furniture with doors and shelves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「橱柜」，有门有搁板，与抽屉不同。

entries.definition: A large box with a lid, or the part of furniture holding drawers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「箱；柜」，可指带抽屉的柜体。

entries.definition: A separate section inside a larger space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「隔间」，指大空间内分出的区块。

normalIntro.en: These hooks pair the sliding action with the -er ending and the pronunciation trap.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把推拉动作、-er 后缀与读音陷阱配在一起。

normal.en: A drawer is the box that gets drawn out, named after the action.
normal.cn: 抽屉就是被「拉出来」的那个箱子，因动作而得名。

normal.en: The -er ending also gives the person who draws a cheque.
normal.cn: -er 词尾还能给出「开支票的人」。

normal.en: The verb sounds its w, but the furniture word does not.
normal.cn: 动词里 w 发音，家具这个词里则不发音。

normal.en: Chest of drawers is the whole piece, not one box.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 指整件柜子，而不是单个抽屉。

normal.en: Out of the top drawer is an old way of saying upper class.
normal.cn: out of the top drawer 是旧时说「出身上层」的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open with a soft scrape.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开时那声轻轻的摩擦响。

abstract.en: Picture a jumble of old receipts under folded clothes.
abstract.cn: 想象叠好的衣服下面压着一堆旧票据。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring hidden in the top drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙藏在最上面的抽屉里。

examples.en: She pulled open the drawer and found an old photo.
examples.cn: 她拉开抽屉，找到一张旧照片。

examples.en: The desk has three drawers on the left side.
examples.cn: 这张书桌左侧有三个抽屉。

examples.en: The drawer of the note is responsible for the payment.
examples.cn: 这张票据的开票人负责付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: draw 是「拉」，-er 是「东西」，被拉出来的那个箱子就是「抽屉」；同样是 -er，也能指「开票的人」。

root: 由 draw（拉、画）加施事后缀 -er 构成。字面是「被拉动的东西」或「做这个动作的人」，因此既指可推拉的抽屉，也指开票人或制图者。draw 源自中古英语 draught 背后的古英语 dragan（拖、拉）。

sensesIntro.en: The -er form splits into a thing that is drawn and a person who draws.
sensesIntro.cn: 带 -er 的形式分成两路：被拉动的东西，与做这个动作的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer sliding out with a soft scrape.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉带着摩擦声滑出来。

branches.en: THE BOX: the thing being pulled out takes the action's name.
branches.cn: 箱体线：被拉出来的那个物件沿用了动作之名，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the -er ending marks whoever draws lines or bills.
branches.cn: 人物线：-er 词尾标示画线条或开票据的人，即第二个义项。

branches.en: One suffix produces both a thing and a person, which is why the meanings look unrelated.
branches.cn: 同一个后缀既产出物也产出人，所以两个义项看起来毫不相干。

branches.en: Storage: a drawer keeps small things out of sight but within reach.
branches.cn: 收纳线：抽屉把小东西藏起来，却又伸手可及。

branches.en: Trade: the drawer of a bill is the person who puts the payment in motion.
branches.cn: 票据线：开票人就是让这笔付款动起来的人。

intro.en: Drawer is a clean build of one verb and one suffix, though its two senses split widely.
intro.cn: drawer 是一个动词加一个后缀的干净构词，但两个义项分得很远。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; draw is Germanic and -er is a native English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁成分：draw 属日耳曼语，-er 是英语本土后缀。

items.example: Draw is the base of drawer.
items.exampleCN: draw 是 drawer 的基础词。

items.meaning: a thing or person that does

items.example: A drawer slides on a track.
A cupboard has doors, a drawer slides.
items.exampleCN: 橱柜有门，抽屉则是滑动。

由 draw 加 -ing 构成，义为「图画；绘画」，与 drawer 同一词族

definition_zh: 梦；梦想；理想；做梦；梦想；幻想
definition_en: images and stories the mind produces during sleep, or something you deeply hope for
core_image: 闭眼后眼前浮现的一片模糊又明亮的画面
scene: 清晨醒来，她还能记起夜里走过的那条不存在的街道。I had a strange dream about a house with no doors.
sceneCN: 这里 dream 是「梦」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我做了一个关于没有门的房子的怪梦。

derivatives.zh: 由 dream 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「做梦的人；空想家」
由 dream 加 -y 构成，义为「梦幻的；心不在焉的」
由 dream 加 -less 构成，义为「无梦的」

senses.title: Images seen during sleep
senses.definition: a series of pictures, events, or feelings that happen in your mind while you sleep
senses.definitionCN: 睡着时在脑中发生的一连串画面、事件或感受
senses.example: I had a dream about falling from a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 我梦见自己从桥上掉下来。
senses.why: The oldest English word for this, swefn, was replaced by dream, which first meant joy or music and then took over the sleeping vision.
senses.whyCN: 英语里表示此义的古词 swefn 被 dream 取代；dream 最初指「喜悦、乐声」，后来接管了睡梦这一含义。

senses.title: Something you deeply hope for
senses.definition: a strong wish for something you want very much to happen
senses.definitionCN: 对极想实现之事的强烈愿望
senses.example: Her dream was to run a small bakery by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 她的梦想是在海边开一家小面包店。
senses.why: A daytime vision of the future looks like the pictures of sleep, so the same word covers deep hopes.
senses.whyCN: 白天对未来的想象与睡梦中的画面很像，于是同一个词也覆盖深切的愿望。

senses.title: A perfect or ideal thing
senses.definition: used to describe something that is exactly what one could wish for
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容完全合乎心愿的事物
senses.example: The little flat was a dream to live in.
senses.exampleCN: 那间小公寓住起来简直是理想之选。
senses.why: What matches a wish perfectly feels as good as a pleasant dream, so the word turns into a praise.
senses.whyCN: 完全符合心愿的东西，感觉就像一场美梦，于是这个词又变成一种称赞。

senses.title: To see images while asleep
senses.definition: to experience pictures and events in your mind during sleep
senses.definitionCN: 睡着时在脑中经历画面与事件
senses.example: She dreamed about the sea almost every night.
senses.exampleCN: 她几乎每晚都梦见大海。
senses.why: The noun came first, and the verb simply names the act of having those sleeping pictures.
senses.whyCN: 先有名词，动词只是把「经历那些睡中画面」这个动作命名出来。

senses.title: To hope strongly for something
senses.definition: to wish for something so strongly that it occupies your thoughts
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地希望某事，以至于它占满你的思绪
senses.example: He dreams of opening his own workshop one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他梦想有一天开一家自己的工坊。
senses.why: Because daytime longing mirrors the pictures of sleep, the verb also means to wish intensely.
senses.whyCN: 因为白天的渴望与睡梦画面互为镜像，动词也就表示「强烈地盼望」。

intro.en: Dream is an English word of uncertain origin that displaced the older word swefn in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: dream 是来源不太确定的英语词，在中世纪取代了更早的 swefn。

items.en: Dream first meant joy or merry sound, not a sleeping vision; the modern sense came later.
items.cn: 古英语 dream 最初指喜悦或欢闹的声音，并非睡中之景，现代义出现较晚。

items.en: Swefn was the ordinary Old English word for a dream during sleep.
items.cn: swefn 才是古英语里表示睡梦的常用词。

items.en: Dream took over the sleeping sense, though how this happened is uncertain and several explanations exist.
items.cn: dream 接管了睡梦义，但这一转变如何发生并不确定，存在多种解释。

items.en: Dream was fully established for sleep visions, and the hope sense followed.
items.cn: dream 已完全确立为睡梦之义，随后又长出愿望义。

items.en: The noun and verb spread to ambition, ideal things and phrases such as dream come true.
items.cn: 名词与动词扩展到抱负、理想之物，以及 dream come true 一类短语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates sleeping visions from waking hopes.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把睡中之景与清醒时的愿望分开。

entries.definition: A person who dreams a lot, or one with impractical hopes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「做梦的人；空想家」，由 dream 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Pleasantly unreal, or absent-minded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「梦幻的；心不在焉的」，由 dream 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: The older past tense, still used in British English.
entries.definitionCN: dream 的不规则过去式，英式英语中仍在使用。

entries.definition: A frightening dream.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「噩梦」，是 dream 的负面版本。

entries.definition: An image seen in the mind, often with a forward-looking sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幻象；愿景」，多指清醒时所见的图景。

entries.definition: A strong desire to achieve something, usually with effort behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抱负」，比 dream 更强调付诸行动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the two sides of dream apart: the sleeping picture and the waking wish.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 dream 的两面分开：睡中的画面与清醒时的愿望。

normal.en: Old English dream meant joy, and swept over the old word for sleeping visions.
normal.cn: 古英语 dream 本指喜悦，后来覆盖了原先表示睡梦的那个词。

normal.en: Dreamt is the old past form that British speakers still keep.
normal.cn: dreamt 是古老的过去式，英式英语仍保留它。

normal.en: Dream of and dream about split the hope sense from the sleeping sense.
normal.cn: dream of 偏愿望，dream about 偏睡梦内容。

normal.en: A pipe dream is a dream you can never smoke.
normal.cn: pipe dream 是一场永远吸不到嘴的空想。

normal.en: Dream come true works because the wish and the picture have fused.
normal.cn: dream come true 成立，是因为愿望与画面已经合成一件事。

abstract.en: Picture a bright street that does not exist anywhere on the map.
abstract.cn: 想象一条地图上根本不存在的明亮街道。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window that perfectly matches what you wanted.
abstract.cn: 想象橱窗里的东西完全合乎你的心愿。

abstract.en: Picture someone staring out of a bus window, far away in thought.
abstract.cn: 想象有人望着公交窗外，心神早已飘远。

examples.en: She dreamed the same dream three nights in a row.
examples.cn: 她连续三晚做同一个梦。

examples.en: His dream is to teach in a village school.
examples.cn: 他的梦想是在乡村学校教书。

examples.en: The garden looks like a dream in early summer.
examples.cn: 初夏时这座花园美得像梦境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹梦」——夜里闭上眼，画面像被轻轻吹起来一样浮现，就是 dream 的「梦、梦想」。

root: 古英语 dream 最初意为「喜悦、欢闹之声」，睡梦义原本由 swefn 承担。中世纪 dream 逐渐接管睡梦义，具体演变原因尚不确定，存在多种解释。随后由「睡中画面」引申为「梦想、理想」，再引申为「完美之物」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with pictures during sleep, then lends itself to hopes, ideal things, and the acts of both.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从睡中的画面出发，再借给愿望、理想之物，以及这两者的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright blurred scene appearing behind closed eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：闭眼之后浮起的一片明亮而模糊的场景。

branches.en: SLEEP: the noun and the verb both belong to the sleeping picture.
branches.cn: 睡眠线：名词与动词都属于睡中的画面，即第一、四个义项。

branches.en: HOPE: the same picture moved into daylight becomes a goal and a longing.
branches.cn: 愿望线：同一幅画面搬到白天，就成了目标与渴望，即第二、五个义项。

branches.en: IDEAL: what matches a wish perfectly is praised as a dream.
branches.cn: 完美线：完全合乎心愿的事物被夸作 dream，即第三个义项。

branches.en: Sleeping pictures and waking hopes share the same vivid, unreal quality.
branches.cn: 睡中画面与白日期盼，共享同样鲜明而不真实的质感。

branches.en: A dream job and a dream flat are hopes that already look achieved.
branches.cn: 理想的工作与理想的公寓，是看起来已经实现的愿望。

intro.en: Dream is a native English word with a busy family of endings and compounds.
intro.cn: dream 是英语本族词，接词尾与复合都很活跃。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the word is English and its earlier history is genuinely uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先；这个词属英语，其更早的历史确实不确定。

items.example: The old sense was joy, not sleep.
Nightmare is the dark twin of dream.
items.exampleCN: nightmare 是 dream 的黑暗孪生。

derivatives.zh: 由 dream 加 -er 构成，义为「做梦的人；空想家」
由 dream 加 -y 构成，义为「梦幻的」

definition_zh: 连衣裙；服装；穿着；打扮；包扎；整理；调味
definition_en: a woman's one-piece garment, or to put clothes on and prepare something carefully
core_image: 一件裙子被平铺在床上，衣摆垂到床沿
scene: 出门前她对着镜子换了三次衣服，最后还是选了那条深色的。She wore a plain black dress to the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 dress 是「连衣裙」（第 1 个义项）；句意是她穿了一条素净的黑裙去面试。

pos.zh: 动词：给……穿衣；包扎；整理；调味

derivatives.zh: 由 dress 加 -ing 构成，义为「调味汁；敷料」
由 dress 加 -er 构成，义为「梳妆台；着装者」
由 dress 加 -y 构成，义为「讲究穿着的；正式的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 dress 构成，义为「脱衣」

senses.title: A woman's one-piece garment
senses.definition: a piece of clothing for a woman or girl that covers the body and part of the legs in one piece
senses.definitionCN: 女性穿的、上衣与裙摆连成一体的服装
senses.example: She bought a cotton dress for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一条夏天穿的棉裙。
senses.why: The word came from a verb meaning to arrange or prepare, and a dress is the garment arranged on the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「整理、准备」的动词，连衣裙就是被「整理」到身上的那件衣物。

senses.title: Clothing in general, or a style of it
senses.definition: clothes of a particular kind, or the way people wear them
senses.definitionCN: 某一类衣物，或人们的穿着方式
senses.example: The invitation says formal dress is required.
senses.exampleCN: 邀请函上写着须着正装。
senses.why: From one garment the word widened to the whole arrangement of clothes a person puts on.
senses.whyCN: 从一件衣服出发，这个词扩展到一个人穿在身上的整套「整理好的」衣物。

senses.title: To put clothes on someone
senses.definition: to put clothes on yourself or on another person
senses.definitionCN: 给自己或给别人穿上衣服
senses.example: She dressed the children before the school van came.
senses.exampleCN: 校车来之前她给孩子们穿好衣服。
senses.why: Dressing someone is literally arranging them, which is the oldest sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 给别人穿衣，字面上就是把人「整理好」，这正是这个动词最古老的用法。

senses.title: To clean and cover a wound
senses.definition: to clean a wound and cover it with a bandage
senses.definitionCN: 清洁伤口并用绷带包好
senses.example: A nurse dressed the cut on his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 一名护士给他胳膊上的伤口做了包扎。
senses.why: Treating a wound is also preparing and arranging it properly, so the same verb serves medicine.
senses.whyCN: 处理伤口同样是把伤口「整理妥当」，所以同一个动词也用于医疗。

senses.title: To prepare food with a sauce
senses.definition: to add oil, vinegar, or sauce to a salad or dish before serving
senses.definitionCN: 在上桌前给沙拉或菜肴加油、醋或酱汁
senses.example: Dress the salad just before you serve it.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前再给沙拉调味。
senses.why: Preparing a dish for the table is another act of arranging, which is why food is also dressed.
senses.whyCN: 把菜准备上桌也是一次「整理」，所以食物也能被 dress。

senses.title: To arrange or prepare something
senses.definition: to prepare a material such as stone or timber by shaping it
senses.definitionCN: 通过加工使石材、木材等材料成形
senses.example: The workers dressed the stone before laying it.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在铺砌之前先把石料加工好。
senses.why: This is the verb's original meaning kept alive in crafts: making something fit and orderly.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个动词最本初的意思，在手工行业里保留了下来：把材料弄整齐、弄合用。

intro.en: Dress came through Old French from Latin directus, straight or arranged, so the core idea is setting something in order.
intro.cn: dress 经古法语来自拉丁语 directus（直的、被整理的），核心意思是「把东西摆整齐」。

items.en: Directus meant straight or set right, from the verb dirigere, to guide or align.
items.cn: directus 意为「直的、被摆正的」，源自动词 dirigere（引导、排成直线）。

items.en: Drecier meant to set upright, to arrange, or to prepare.
items.cn: drecier 意为「竖正、整理、准备」。

items.en: English dress first meant to arrange or prepare, including preparing a table or a wound.
items.cn: 英语 dress 最初意为「整理、准备」，包括准备餐桌或处理伤口。

items.en: The clothing sense developed as arranging a person came to mean putting clothes on them.
items.cn: 整理一个人逐渐变成「给人穿衣」，衣着义由此发展出来。

items.en: The noun settled on a one-piece woman's garment, while the verb kept its wider preparing senses.
items.cn: 名词固定指女性连身裙，动词则保留更宽的「整理、加工」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates garments from clothing in general.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把「连衣裙」与「泛指衣物」分开。

entries.definition: A sauce for salads, or a bandage for a wound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调味汁；敷料」，由 dress 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A piece of furniture with a mirror, or a person who dresses others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「梳妆台；着装者」，由 dress 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To take off one's clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「脱衣」，由 un- 加 dress 构成。

entries.definition: A long formal dress, worn on special occasions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长礼服」，多用于正式场合。

entries.definition: Clothes in general, as a mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣物（总称）」，不可数，与 dress 的第二义项相近。

entries.definition: Clothing for a role, a period, or a festival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏服；特定场合的服装」，强调角色或场合。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the idea of arranging and follow it to clothes, wounds, salad and stone.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从「整理」出发，一路跟到衣服、伤口、沙拉与石料。

normal.en: Directus meant set straight, so dress is about putting things in order.
normal.cn: directus 意为「摆正」，所以 dress 的核心就是「弄整齐」。

normal.en: Putting clothes on a person is arranging them, which is why the verb and the garment share a word.
normal.cn: 给人穿衣就是把人整理好，所以动词与衣物共用一个词。

normal.en: Dress a wound and dress a salad both arrange something for use.
normal.cn: 包扎伤口与给沙拉调味，都是把东西整理到可用状态。

normal.en: Dress code fixes the arrangement everyone must follow.
normal.cn: dress code 规定的是所有人都要遵守的那套「整理方式」。

normal.en: Undress simply reverses the arranging.
normal.cn: undress 就是把这个整理过程倒过来。

abstract.en: Picture a dark dress spread flat across a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条深色裙子平铺在床上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand smoothing a bandage over a cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把绷带抚平贴在伤口上。

abstract.en: Picture oil being poured slowly over green leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象油缓缓浇在绿叶上。

examples.en: The dress in the window is too expensive for me.
examples.cn: 橱窗里那条裙子对我来说太贵了。

examples.en: He dressed quickly and ran for the train.
examples.cn: 他迅速穿好衣服去赶火车。

examples.en: The nurse dressed the wound with clean cloth.
examples.cn: 护士用干净的布给伤口做了包扎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽丝」——拽起丝质裙摆整理好再穿，dress 既是「连衣裙」，也是「穿衣、整理」。

root: 经古法语 drecier 来自拉丁语 directus（直的、被摆正的），源头是动词 dirigere（引导、排直）。本义是「整理、摆正、准备」，因此既指给人穿衣，也指包扎伤口、给食物调味、加工石料；名词则由「整理好的衣物」固定为女性的连身裙。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of arranging spreads over clothes, wounds, food and materials, while the noun narrows to a garment.
sensesIntro.cn: 「整理」这一个想法铺开到衣服、伤口、食物与材料上，而名词则收窄为一件衣物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garment laid out flat and smoothed into order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件衣服被平铺展开，抚平整理。

branches.en: CLOTHES: the noun names a single garment and then clothing in general.
branches.cn: 衣物线：名词先指单件裙装，再泛指衣着，即第一、二个义项。

branches.en: ACTION: arranging a person turns into putting clothes on them.
branches.cn: 动作线：把人整理好，变成给人穿衣，即第三个义项。

branches.en: MEDICINE: a wound is also prepared and covered.
branches.cn: 医疗线：伤口同样要被整理与覆盖，即第四个义项。

branches.en: CRAFT: food and stone are both arranged before use.
branches.cn: 工艺线：食物与石料在上用之前都要被整理，即第五、六个义项。

branches.en: Dressing a child and dressing a wound both mean making something fit and covered.
branches.cn: 给孩子穿衣与给伤口包扎，都是让对象变得妥当并被覆好。

intro.en: Dress is a borrowed stem that takes native English endings and a negative prefix.
intro.cn: dress 是借来的词干，可接英语本土词尾与否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin directus stands at the head of the family; the English forms grew through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 directus 位于这个词族的最上游，英语形式经法语长出。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the ultimate source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是最初的来源。

items.meaning: a thing or person that does
